sections.body: Ethernet switching taught you how a switch learns addresses and forwards frames. VLANs define which Layer 2 network those decisions belong to. In this chapter, you will create VLANs, assign host-facing ports, distinguish data from voice traffic, and diagnose a connected port that serves the wrong network. You will also check the power requirements of phones, access points and other powered endpoints.

sections.title: Separate Layer 2 networks with VLANs
sections.body:
A **virtual LAN (VLAN)** is a logical Layer 2 broadcast domain. In an ordinary VLAN-aware switching configuration, an Ethernet broadcast received in VLAN 10 is forwarded only to eligible forwarding ports in VLAN 10, excluding the receiving port. It is not copied into VLAN 20 merely because both VLANs use the same physical switch.

The switch learns source MAC addresses in a VLAN context and looks up destinations within that context. Unknown unicast flooding remains inside the applicable VLAN. Multicast forwarding may also be controlled by multicast features, so do not use the shortcut that every multicast frame always goes to every port.

A **subnet** is an IP-layer address grouping determined by a prefix or mask. A VLAN and a subnet are related design choices, but they are not the same object. A common campus design uses one IP subnet per VLAN. That gives hosts a consistent local network and a router or multilayer-switch interface to use as their gateway.

```diagram
{"type":"topology","title":"Two VLANs on one switch","caption":"An ARP broadcast from PC-A reaches PC-B in VLAN 10, while the VLAN 20 ports remain a separate Layer 2 network.","nodes":[{"id":"A","kind":"pc","label":"PC-A","sub":"192.168.10.11/24","x":1,"y":1},{"id":"B","kind":"pc","label":"PC-B","sub":"192.168.10.12/24","x":1,"y":5},{"id":"S","kind":"switch","label":"SW1","x":6,"y":3},{"id":"C","kind":"pc","label":"PC-C","sub":"192.168.20.13/24","x":11,"y":1},{"id":"D","kind":"printer","label":"Printer","sub":"192.168.20.20/24","x":11,"y":5}],"links":[{"from":"A","to":"S","toLabel":"Fa0/1 · VLAN 10"},{"from":"B","to":"S","toLabel":"Fa0/2 · VLAN 10"},{"from":"S","to":"C","fromLabel":"Fa0/3 · VLAN 20"},{"from":"S","to":"D","fromLabel":"Fa0/4 · VLAN 20"}]}
```

Consider PC-A at `192.168.10.11/24` and PC-B at `192.168.10.12/24`. Both regard the other address as local, so PC-A uses ARP for PC-B rather than sending the packet to a gateway. If a technician moves PC-B's switchport into VLAN 20 without changing its IP configuration, the ARP request remains in VLAN 10. The physical link can be healthy while the host is attached to the wrong broadcast domain.

Conversely, putting two hosts in the same VLAN does not force their IP configurations to be compatible. If their addresses and masks place them in different subnets, a router or other appropriate IP configuration may be needed. Check both VLAN membership and IP addressing before diagnosing a routing failure.

VLANs reduce broadcast scope and provide useful segmentation. They do not automatically supply a firewall policy. Inter-VLAN routing is introduced in Chapter 11; once routing is enabled, access lists or other controls determine which routed communications are allowed.

:::facts
- VLAN membership is Layer 2; a subnet mask determines a host's IP network membership.
- On the Catalyst platforms used here, normal-range VLANs are `1–1005`; extended-range VLANs are `1006–4094`.
- VLAN `0` is used for priority-tagged frames rather than ordinary VLAN membership; `4095` is reserved. Neither is an ordinary configurable user VLAN.
- VLAN `1` and legacy VLANs `1002–1005` exist by default on the lab Catalyst switch. Use ordinary user VLANs such as `10`, `20` and `30` in this exercise.
- `switchport mode access` fixes the port's mode; `switchport access vlan 10` sets its data VLAN. These are separate settings.
- A deleted data VLAN does not automatically move assigned ports back into VLAN 1.
:::

sections.title: Create and verify the VLAN database
sections.body:
A VLAN's number is its forwarding identity. Its name is an administrative label. Two switches can use different names for VLAN 10, but that does not create different VLAN tags; keep names consistent to make the documentation easier to follow.

| VLAN range | Use in this course |
|---|---|
| `1` | Factory-default VLAN; avoid treating it as an automatically secured management network |
| `2–1001` | Ordinary normal-range user VLANs |
| `1002–1005` | Legacy reserved VLANs displayed by the lab Catalyst image |
| `1006–4094` | Extended-range VLANs; support and persistence depend on platform/VTP behavior |

Create the VLAN before assigning endpoints. This makes the sequence explicit and avoids relying on a particular image to create a missing VLAN as a side effect of a port command.

```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# vlan 10
SW1(config-vlan)# name USERS
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# vlan 20
SW1(config-vlan)# name PRINTERS
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# vlan 30
SW1(config-vlan)# name VOICE
SW1(config-vlan)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
```

Normal-range VLANs on the referenced Catalyst platforms are maintained in the VLAN database, commonly `flash:vlan.dat`. Depending on VTP mode, VLAN definitions may also appear in the running and startup configurations. Port assignments are interface configuration. For this course, verify both the VLAN database and the interface configuration; a configuration-file view alone is not the whole picture.

**VTP**, the VLAN Trunking Protocol, can distribute VLAN definitions between switches. It is not required to configure each switch manually in these labs. Detailed VTP administration is outside this chapter's target. The relevant operational lesson is that an existing switch may retain VLAN information independently of an erased startup configuration; do not assume an erase-and-reload sequence cleared every file.

Deleting VLAN 20 removes its ordinary data forwarding domain. Ports assigned to it retain the configured VLAN number and become inactive for that data VLAN. Recreate the VLAN or deliberately reassign the ports to the correct existing VLAN. A separate configured voice VLAN on a phone port must be considered independently; do not infer that every kind of traffic on the physical port must fail.

sections.title: Configure an access port
sections.body:
A conventional **access port** carries one data VLAN for an endpoint that sends untagged Ethernet frames. On reception, the switch classifies those frames into the access VLAN. When it sends ordinary data frames back toward that endpoint, they are untagged. The endpoint does not need to know the switch's VLAN number.

```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/2
SW1(config-if)# description User workstation
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/2 switchport
```

Do not assume that the factory administrative mode is always static access. Some Catalyst images default to a dynamic mode that can negotiate a trunk. Setting `switchport mode access` removes that ambiguity for a simple host-facing port. Chapter 10 explains dynamic trunk negotiation and static trunks.

The **administrative mode** records the configured intent; the **operational mode** records how the interface is currently functioning. Also read the access VLAN's status. A configured value of 10 accompanied by `Inactive` is different from an active VLAN 10. The interface may still show physical connectivity in either case.

```output SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/2 switchport — representative excerpt
Name: Fa0/2
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: static access  ← explicitly configured access mode
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (USERS)         ← the data VLAN
Voice VLAN: none
```

A phone/voice configuration is an important exception to the simplified description of an access port as carrying only untagged traffic. The next section covers it. Do not extrapolate this simple-PC example into a rule that any tagged frame on any access port must always be discarded.

sections.title: Carry voice and data on a phone port
sections.body:
An IP phone can contain a small Ethernet switch: one port faces the access switch, and another connects a PC. A common Cisco deployment keeps the PC's data in the access VLAN while the phone's voice traffic uses a separate **voice VLAN**.

```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# description Phone with attached PC
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# switchport voice vlan 30
SW1(config-if)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if)# end
```

For the configured tagged-voice behavior, the PC's frames arrive untagged and are classified into VLAN 10. The phone sends its voice-VLAN frames tagged with VLAN ID 30. The port remains an access port with the voice-VLAN feature; it is not configured as a general-purpose trunk carrying an arbitrary list of VLANs.

| Traffic presented to the switch | Classification in this example |
|---|---|
| Untagged PC data relayed through the phone | Access VLAN 10 |
| Phone traffic correctly tagged for the configured voice VLAN | Voice VLAN 30 |
| Phone discovery/control traffic | Interpret by the protocol; it does not prove that a voice call is established |

Cisco phones can learn voice policy through CDP. LLDP-MED is another supported method on suitable phones and switches, and a phone can have manually provisioned settings. Therefore, a missing CDP neighbor is a reason to inspect discovery and provisioning; it is not proof that every phone must fall back to the data VLAN. The receiving device's capabilities and configuration matter.

Verify that the voice VLAN exists and is active, the port names the intended data and voice VLANs, and the phone has power. A working data connection through the phone does not prove that voice addressing, call control or registration works. Those services are outside this switching exercise. Likewise, discovering a phone is not proof that it has obtained a voice-VLAN lease.

Some Catalyst images automatically enable PortFast when voice VLAN is configured. Chapter 15 explains edge-port behavior and protection. Do not infer that one port-security address limit fits every phone-plus-PC deployment: allowed addresses, VLANs and device behavior need a separate design, taught in Chapter 16.

sections.title: Check PoE capability and the power budget
sections.body:
**Power over Ethernet (PoE)** supplies power over supported copper Ethernet cabling. The switch or injector is the **power sourcing equipment (PSE)**; the phone, AP or other endpoint is the **powered device (PD)**. A non-PoE Ethernet port cannot be made into a PoE port by adding a configuration command.

There are two separate capacity checks. First, the port, cable and powered device must support the required power level. Second, the switch's shared budget must have enough allocation remaining. A switch with many PoE+ ports does not necessarily have enough total power to run every port at its maximum simultaneously.

| Standard | Maximum PSE power | Power available at the PD under the standard's limits |
|---|---:|---:|
| IEEE 802.3af | 15.4 W | 12.95 W |
| IEEE 802.3at (PoE+) | 30 W | 25.5 W |
| IEEE 802.3bt Type 3 | Up to 60 W | Up to 51 W |
| IEEE 802.3bt Type 4 | Up to 90 W | Up to 71.3 W |

The difference accounts for permitted losses; source power and device power are not interchangeable. The higher figures require the corresponding supported equipment and conditions. For exam problems, use the supplied requirement and state whether it is a PSE allocation or power needed at the device.

For example, suppose a switch has a usable PoE allocation budget of 370 W. Ten phones reserve 6.3 W each, leaving `370 − 63 = 307 W`. If each additional AP requires a 30 W allocation, ten APs fit because `10 × 30 = 300 W`; eleven do not. This is allocation arithmetic. A momentary measured draw below the reserved value does not automatically create permission to oversubscribe the budget.

```ios SW2
SW2# show power inline
SW2# configure terminal
SW2(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/1
SW2(config-if)# power inline auto
SW2(config-if)# end
SW2# show power inline
```

Use this command family only on a supporting PoE model. `auto` enables the supported detection/allocation behavior; `never` disables PoE on the port. Where supported, `power inline auto max 7000` specifies a 7000 mW, or 7 W, maximum. Supported limits and enforcement behavior are platform-specific. Reducing that limit is not a general fix for a device that genuinely needs more power.

:::trap A connected Ethernet cable does not prove enough power
Check PSE capability, PD requirements, administrative PoE state, cabling and the shared budget. A power-denied indication needs those checks; an arbitrary VLAN change does not increase the power budget. A powered AP can also run with reduced features when its available power is insufficient for its full operating mode.
:::

sections.title: Choose the port from the endpoint requirements
sections.body:
Begin with what the endpoint presents on the wire. Does it send one untagged network or several tagged networks? Does it need PoE? Does it bridge traffic from other devices? Does it explicitly support a negotiated link bundle? These questions are more reliable than applying a desktop template to every object called a host.

| Endpoint requirement | Starting connectivity choice | Continue with |
|---|---|---|
| PC, printer or IoT device using one untagged network | Access port in its intended VLAN; PoE only where required | Verification in this chapter |
| Cisco phone with a PC behind it | Data access VLAN plus the intended voice VLAN | Phone provisioning and power checks |
| AP carrying its own untagged management traffic and tunneling client traffic to a controller | An access VLAN can serve that uplink | Wireless architecture in Chapter 37 |
| AP or virtual host presenting several VLANs on one uplink | A trunk whose tagging matches the endpoint | Trunk configuration in Chapter 10 |
| Server or appliance configured for LACP | Compatible bundle at both ends | EtherChannel in Chapter 13 |
| Appliance that bridges other devices' frames | Review VLANs, MAC sources and loop behavior before applying edge assumptions | Chapters 14–16 |

This chapter teaches the selection reasoning and the access/voice configuration. It does not ask you to configure LACP or spanning-tree guards before you understand them. [Trunks](#/chapter/trunks-dtp), [EtherChannel](#/chapter/etherchannel), [STP protection](#/chapter/stp-protection) and [Layer 2 security](#/chapter/layer2-security) provide those complete procedures.

sections.title: Verify and troubleshoot
sections.body:
Use a short evidence chain: physical state, operational port mode, active VLAN membership, learned MAC addresses, then host addressing and reachability. Each command answers a different part of that chain.

| Command or test | What it establishes | What it does not establish alone |
|---|---|---|
| `show interfaces status` | Link state and a summary of the port's VLAN/mode | Correct host IP settings or application access |
| `show vlan brief` | Defined VLANs, status and displayed port membership | The full state of trunks or host reachability |
| `show interfaces fa0/1 switchport` | Administrative/operational mode and data/voice settings | Phone registration or a complete end-to-end VLAN path |
| `show mac address-table` | Where source addresses have been learned by VLAN | A successful application session |
| `show power inline` | Reported PoE state and allocation information | Correct VLAN/IP configuration |

For a moved workstation, compare its documented VLAN with the actual port. If its MAC is learned in VLAN 20 but its address plan belongs to VLAN 10, do not change the host address merely to fit the mistaken port. Restore the intended assignment, generate fresh traffic, and verify the MAC is learned in the correct VLAN.

For a newly created or restored VLAN, check that it is active before testing again. On a single-switch lab, same-VLAN peers with compatible addresses should communicate once links and forwarding state are ready. Different VLANs need an appropriate Layer 3 path; failure between them is expected when no router is present.

sections.title: Exam focus
sections.body:
- Distinguish a VLAN, an IP subnet, a physical link and a host's gateway.
- Create and name VLANs; configure and verify static access-port membership.
- Explain the result of a missing or deleted data VLAN without assuming every traffic type on the port fails.
- Read administrative versus operational mode and VLAN status from switchport output.
- Explain untagged data and tagged voice for the stated phone configuration.
- Choose access, voice or later trunk/bundle work from the endpoint's actual requirements.
- Check PoE capability and budget separately, using the correct units and allocation assumptions.
- Diagnose from VLAN, MAC-table, interface and host evidence rather than link lights alone.

lab.title: Build data and voice VLANs, identify assignment faults, and verify power requirements
devices: 1 × Cisco 7960 IP phone with its external power adapter
lab.intro:
The required switching work uses a new Packet Tracer project. The PoE budget exercise uses supplied evidence, with an optional supporting-switch observation. No router, DHCP server or call-control server is needed. You will verify switching and port configuration; this lab does not claim to establish a working voice call.


Practice revised September 2026. If you completed an earlier version, repeat the revised exercise and update its checkmarks.
lab.topology:
```diagram
{"type":"topology","title":"Data and voice access lab","caption":"PC-A connects through the powered phone; PC-A and PC-B use VLAN 10, while PC-C and the printer use VLAN 20.","nodes":[{"id":"A","kind":"pc","label":"PC-A","sub":"192.168.10.11/24","x":1,"y":1},{"id":"PH","kind":"phone","label":"Phone","sub":"External power","x":4,"y":1},{"id":"B","kind":"pc","label":"PC-B","sub":"192.168.10.12/24","x":1,"y":5},{"id":"S","kind":"switch","label":"SW1","sub":"2960-24TT","x":7,"y":3},{"id":"C","kind":"pc","label":"PC-C","sub":"192.168.20.13/24","x":11,"y":1},{"id":"PR","kind":"printer","label":"Printer","sub":"192.168.20.20/24","x":11,"y":5}],"links":[{"from":"A","to":"PH","toLabel":"PC"},{"from":"PH","to":"S","fromLabel":"Switch","toLabel":"Fa0/1"},{"from":"B","to":"S","toLabel":"Fa0/2"},{"from":"S","to":"C","fromLabel":"Fa0/3"},{"from":"S","to":"PR","fromLabel":"Fa0/4"}]}
```

Use copper straight-through cables for every connection. On PC-A, PC-B and PC-C, enter the addresses below under Desktop → IP Configuration. On Printer-PT, use its Config interface/IP settings. Leave gateways and DNS unset for this isolated local-subnet exercise.

| Endpoint | Switch path | Address and mask | Intended VLAN |
|---|---|---|---|
| PC-A Fa0 | Phone PC port → phone Switch port → SW1 Fa0/1 | `192.168.10.11`, `255.255.255.0` | 10 |
| PC-B Fa0 | SW1 Fa0/2 | `192.168.10.12`, `255.255.255.0` | 10 |
| PC-C Fa0 | SW1 Fa0/3 | `192.168.20.13`, `255.255.255.0` | 20 |
| Printer Fa0 | SW1 Fa0/4 | `192.168.20.20`, `255.255.255.0` | 20 |
| Phone | SW1 Fa0/1 | No voice IP service is configured | Voice VLAN 30 |

steps.title: Build and inspect the physical setup
steps.body:
Place the devices and connect the cables. The 2960-24TT in this lab does not supply PoE. Open the phone's Physical tab and connect its external power adapter using the model's power socket. If the interface differs in your Packet Tracer version, inspect the available power module rather than treating the absence of a phone display as a VLAN fault.

Name the switch through its CLI. Decline an initial setup dialog if one appears.

```ios SW1
Switch> enable
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname SW1
SW1(config)# no ip domain-lookup
SW1(config)# end
SW1# show interfaces status
```

:::expected
Fa0/1–Fa0/4 should report physical connectivity once the devices and links are ready. The phone must have power for its internal data path to operate. Wait for ordinary forwarding state to settle; do not assume an exact number of seconds across simulator versions. No voice registration is expected.
:::

steps.title: Create the VLANs
steps.body:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# vlan 10
SW1(config-vlan)# name USERS
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# vlan 20
SW1(config-vlan)# name PRINTERS
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# vlan 30
SW1(config-vlan)# name VOICE
SW1(config-vlan)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
```

:::expected
VLANs 10, 20 and 30 appear as active. Merely creating them has not yet reassigned the connected data ports. If the new VLANs are missing, correct their creation before moving on to host tests.
:::

steps.title: Assign access ports and test local peers
steps.body:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface range fastethernet0/1 - 2
SW1(config-if-range)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if-range)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if-range)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if-range)# exit
SW1(config)# interface range fastethernet0/3 - 4
SW1(config-if-range)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if-range)# switchport access vlan 20
SW1(config-if-range)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if-range)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
```

Before the first ping, predict PC-A → PC-B, PC-C → printer, and PC-A → PC-C. Give the VLAN and whether routing would be needed. Record the three predictions before testing.

On PC-A, run `ping 192.168.10.12`. On PC-C, run `ping 192.168.20.20`. Then try `ping 192.168.20.13` from PC-A. Inspect the learned addresses:

```ios SW1
SW1# show mac address-table
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/2 switchport
```

:::expected
Same-subnet peers in the same VLAN should communicate after address resolution and forwarding are ready. The cross-VLAN test has no router or configured gateway to carry it and should fail. PC-A and PC-B's source addresses should be learned in VLAN 10 after they send traffic; PC-C and the printer's in VLAN 20. Record actual MAC addresses rather than copying invented values.
:::

steps.title: Configure the voice VLAN
steps.body:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# description Phone and PC-A
SW1(config-if)# switchport voice vlan 30
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/1 switchport
SW1# show vlan brief
```

Repeat PC-A's ping to PC-B. Inspect the phone's displayed network settings if your simulator exposes them.

:::expected
Fa0/1 should show access VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30. PC-A's ordinary data connectivity remains in VLAN 10. Some image output lists the port under both VLANs. This verifies the switch configuration, not a voice lease, call registration or tagged voice payload: those have not been generated by this lab's absent voice services. Record any observed phone VLAN setting separately from that conclusion.
:::

steps.title: Remove a data VLAN and observe the fault
steps.body:
Predict which local pair should fail and which should remain usable. Then delete only the lab's VLAN 20, leaving its access-port assignments in place. Record physical state, VLAN existence and configured membership separately.

```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# no vlan 20
SW1(config)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/3 switchport
```

Repeat PC-C's ping to the printer. Also repeat PC-A's ping to PC-B.

:::expected
The missing VLAN 20 prevents normal data forwarding for its assigned ports, even if their physical links stay connected. Switchport output may label access VLAN 20 as inactive. VLAN 10's local data test should continue working. Do not change the hosts' IP addresses: the deliberate fault is the missing VLAN.
:::

steps.title: Restore the deleted VLAN
steps.body:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# vlan 20
SW1(config-vlan)# name PRINTERS
SW1(config-vlan)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/3 switchport
```

Repeat PC-C's ping to the printer and record fresh MAC-table entries.

:::expected
VLAN 20 is active again; its existing port assignments become usable. The local PC-C-to-printer test should recover when forwarding is ready. This demonstrates the difference between deleting the VLAN and removing an interface's configured VLAN assignment.
:::

steps.title: Move a port into the wrong VLAN
steps.body:
First predict whether an active VLAN and a connected port are enough to reach its intended peer. Leave PC-B at `192.168.10.12/24`, but move its port to VLAN 20.

```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/2
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/2 switchport
```

Try PC-A's ping to PC-B again. Then send a ping from PC-B to PC-A and inspect SW1:

```ios SW1
SW1# show mac address-table interface fastethernet0/2
```

:::expected
The physical link and VLAN 20 can both be active, but PC-B is now in the wrong broadcast domain for its intended peer. Its newly generated source traffic is learned in VLAN 20. Existing ARP entries do not provide a bridge between the two VLANs, so cached addresses do not repair the fault.
:::

steps.title: Restore membership and verify the endpoint plan
steps.body:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/2
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# description PC-B user workstation
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/2 switchport
SW1# show vlan brief
```

Repeat both same-VLAN tests. In your notes, list each endpoint's physical port, data VLAN, optional voice VLAN, address and power source. Explain why this setup needs neither a trunk nor an LACP bundle.

:::expected
PC-A/PC-B and PC-C/printer communication recover independently. Fa0/1 retains data VLAN 10 plus voice VLAN 30; Fa0/2 uses data VLAN 10; Fa0/3–Fa0/4 use data VLAN 20. The lab has one switch and individual host links, so its required tasks stop at access and voice configuration.
:::

steps.title: Interpret a PoE allocation problem
steps.body:
Use this supplied evidence as a paper exercise. A PoE+ switch has a usable allocation budget of 370 W. Ten phones each reserve 6.3 W; ten APs each require 30 W of PSE allocation. A further AP requests 30 W. All cables, per-port limits and device compatibility have already been checked.

Predict the remaining budget before the additional request, whether the request fits, and a suitable correction that does not underpower an existing device.

If your Packet Tracer version supports PoE reporting on a 3650-24PS, you may add SW2 and a compatible powered endpoint to a separate lab segment. Use a supported port such as Gi1/0/1 and inspect:

```ios SW2
SW2> enable
SW2# show power inline
```

Do not expect this extra device's actual budget or draw to match the paper example. If the command is unavailable, finish the paper exercise without claiming a live power measurement.

:::solution
Phones reserve 63 W and the ten APs reserve 300 W, leaving `370 − 63 − 300 = 7 W`. The additional 30 W allocation does not fit. A suitable change is to move an endpoint to a compatible PSE with enough available budget, or provide supported additional power capacity. Do not lower a real 30 W requirement to 7 W merely to make the allocation fit.
:::

steps.title: Save the corrected setup
steps.body:
```ios SW1
SW1# copy running-config startup-config
```

Press Enter at the destination prompt and wait for SW1# to return. Then inspect the saved configuration and the separate VLAN database:

```ios SW1
SW1# show startup-config
SW1# show vlan brief
```

Save the project as `09-data-voice-vlans.pkt`.

:::expected
The final setup contains active VLANs 10, 20 and 30 and the intended port assignments. Neither deliberate fault remains. The configuration save and Packet Tracer project save serve different purposes; keep both.
:::

Before marking completion, submit these observations:

| Outcome | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Initial plan | Three reachability predictions and actual results |
| Access and voice settings | Actual VLAN and switchport output |
| Distinct faults | Missing VLAN versus active-but-wrong membership |
| Recovery | Both local pairs work after each repair |
| Power decision | Both limits and whether evidence was supplied or observed |
| Independent addition | PC-D's membership, fresh MAC and local tests |

lab.troubleshooting:
- **Phone and attached PC both lack a working link:** check the phone's external power and both Ethernet cables first.
- **Connected port, inactive VLAN:** compare the access VLAN with the VLAN database. Restore the intended VLAN before changing IP settings.
- **Active VLAN, but a moved PC cannot reach its peers:** compare documented membership, switchport output and freshly learned source MAC addresses.
- **PC data works through the phone:** this establishes the data path, not phone registration or voice addressing.
- **Different VLANs cannot communicate here:** expected; no Layer 3 forwarding path was configured.
- **PoE command unavailable:** check the model and image. A non-PoE 2960-24TT cannot supply power through configuration.
- **Power denied:** inspect the actual administrative setting, device requirement, per-port capability and remaining shared allocation before choosing a correction.
lab.challenge:
Add PC-D on SW1 Fa0/5 with `192.168.20.25/24`, no gateway, and a straight-through cable. Configure only the settings needed for it to reach PC-C and the printer. Predict whether it can reach PC-A. Then explain on paper what would happen if only PC-D's switchport changed to VLAN 10 while its address stayed unchanged. Write the configuration and predictions before opening the solution; the added endpoint must also leave both original local tests working.

:::solution
Set Fa0/5 to static access mode in VLAN 20 and ensure it is not shut down. PC-D should reach PC-C and the printer after forwarding and address resolution are ready; it has no routed path to PC-A. Moving only its port to VLAN 10 leaves the host's IP configuration inconsistent with the intended VLAN 20 subnet. Restore the port to VLAN 20, verify its learned source address in that VLAN, and save if retaining the extension.
:::

questions.prompt: Which two checks help establish the intended switch-side data/voice configuration? Choose two.
options: Check only that the port is administratively configured as access
Verify that both configured VLANs exist and are active
Treat successful PC data traffic as proof of voice registration
Read the port’s access VLAN and voice VLAN settings
Require the phone port to negotiate a general-purpose trunk
questions.explanation: Start with the VLAN database and the port’s actual data/voice settings. Phone power, provisioning, IP services and registration require their own checks.

whyWrong.0: Access mode alone does not identify whether the intended data and voice VLANs are active.
whyWrong.2: PC traffic does not verify voice addressing or call-control registration.
whyWrong.4: The access-plus-voice feature does not require a general-purpose trunk.

questions.prompt: Which command directly displays a port’s administrative mode, operational mode, access VLAN and voice VLAN?
options: `show mac address-table interface fastethernet0/1`
`show interfaces fastethernet0/1 switchport`
`show ip interface brief`
`show power inline`
questions.explanation: The switchport view puts intended mode, operating mode and VLAN assignments together. Use VLAN and MAC-table commands alongside it for a fuller diagnosis.

whyWrong.0: That shows learned MAC entries rather than all the listed switchport settings.
whyWrong.2: That reports IP/interface state rather than the full data/voice VLAN configuration.
whyWrong.3: That reports PoE information, not all of these VLAN and mode fields.

exhibit.title: SW1# show interfaces fa0/7 switchport — excerpt
exhibit.text:
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (USERS)
Voice VLAN: 30 (Inactive)

questions.prompt: The port is intended to provide data VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30. What switch-side defect is visible, without making assumptions about the phone’s fallback behavior?
options: The phone is proven to have registered in the data VLAN
The data VLAN is inactive because the voice VLAN is missing
The configured voice VLAN is inactive on this switch
The port must be a trunk because a voice VLAN is configured
questions.explanation: The switchport excerpt identifies an inactive voice VLAN. Verify the VLAN database, create or restore the intended VLAN, and then check the phone’s separate power/provisioning/IP state.

whyWrong.0: This output does not establish phone addressing or registration.
whyWrong.1: The excerpt identifies the inactive voice VLAN separately.
whyWrong.3: Access-plus-voice operation does not require general trunk mode.

questions.prompt: Which statement about VLAN 1 is accurate for the Catalyst lab defaults?
options: Its existence means the switch already has secure remote management
It is the default access VLAN and the default native VLAN for trunks
It automatically routes packets between newly created VLANs
It is deleted automatically when another access VLAN is created
questions.explanation: VLAN 1 has default roles on the referenced Catalyst platform. Do not confuse those defaults with static access mode on every port or a complete, secure management configuration.

whyWrong.0: VLAN existence does not create an IP address, SSH service or authentication policy.
whyWrong.2: A VLAN is a Layer 2 domain and does not by itself enable inter-VLAN routing.
whyWrong.3: Creating another VLAN does not delete VLAN 1.

exhibit.title: SW1# show vlan brief — excerpt
exhibit.text:
10 USERS    active Fa0/1
20 PRINTERS active Fa0/2

questions.prompt: PC-A is 192.168.10.11/24 on Fa0/1; PC-B is 192.168.10.12/24 on Fa0/2. Both links are up, and no routing or VLAN translation is configured. Why can they not communicate?
options: Their host addresses belong to different IPv4 subnets
The peers occupy different Layer 2 broadcast domains
The switch needs a management IP to learn either MAC address
Their default gateways must forward the same-subnet ARP request
questions.explanation: The masks make each peer appear local, but ARP and ordinary switching remain within the assigned VLAN. Correct the mistaken VLAN membership rather than inventing a gateway requirement for same-subnet peers.

whyWrong.0: Both addresses belong to 192.168.10.0/24.
whyWrong.2: Layer 2 forwarding does not require a switch management IP.
whyWrong.3: The hosts consider each other on-link; a gateway does not bridge their separate VLAN broadcasts.

exhibit.title: Supplied relevant verification notes
exhibit.text:
SW1 Fa0/4:
 Administrative Mode: static access
 Operational Mode: static access
 Access Mode VLAN: 20 (Inactive)
Complete VLAN database check: VLAN 20 is absent.

questions.prompt: A printer’s address and cable have not changed. Which correction addresses the condition shown for its data VLAN?
options: Recreate the intended VLAN 20 in the VLAN database
Move the printer to VLAN 1 while retaining its address
Change the switch management gateway to the printer
Clear learned MAC entries while leaving VLAN 20 absent
questions.explanation: The port retains an access-VLAN assignment, but that VLAN is inactive. Restore the intended VLAN and verify the local data path; do not change host addressing to hide the switch-side fault.

whyWrong.1: That changes the intended membership instead of restoring the missing VLAN.
whyWrong.2: A management gateway cannot create a Layer 2 VLAN.
whyWrong.3: A dynamic table clear cannot recreate an absent VLAN.

questions.prompt: A phone is provisioned to tag voice traffic with VLAN 30. Its attached PC sends ordinary untagged data. The switchport has access VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30. How are those two traffic types classified?
options: Both traffic types enter VLAN 30 because the phone is the physical neighbor
PC data enters VLAN 30; tagged voice enters VLAN 10
PC data enters VLAN 10; tagged voice enters VLAN 30
Both traffic types enter VLAN 10 because the port remains access mode
questions.explanation: The ordinary PC traffic uses the access VLAN, while correctly tagged phone voice traffic uses the configured voice VLAN. This describes the stated provisioning; it does not claim that every phone automatically obtains those settings.

whyWrong.0: The configured access VLAN still classifies ordinary untagged PC data.
whyWrong.1: This reverses the data and voice assignments.
whyWrong.3: The voice-VLAN feature permits the stated tagged voice behavior on an access port.

questions.prompt: An AP requires 25 W available at the powered device. Considering the standard limits below, what is the lowest listed PoE standard that can supply it?
options: IEEE 802.3at, with up to 25.5 W available at the PD
IEEE 802.3af, with up to 12.95 W available at the PD
IEEE 802.3bt Type 3, as the first standard above 25 W at the PD
IEEE 802.3bt Type 4, as the first standard above 25 W at the PD
questions.explanation: Compare power needed at the device with device-side capability, not just the switch-port source rating. 802.3at supplies up to 25.5 W at the PD under its specified conditions.

whyWrong.1: The requirement exceeds the device-side capability of 802.3af.
whyWrong.2: Type 3 can supply more power, but 802.3at already meets 25 W.
whyWrong.3: Type 4 is not the lowest standard that meets this requirement.

questions.prompt: A switch has a usable 370 W PoE allocation budget and 24 powered ports. Ten phones reserve 6.3 W each. Each additional AP requires 30 W of allocation at the PSE. How many APs fit within the remaining power and port capacity?
options: 9 APs, because every phone reserves a full 15.4 W
11 APs, because 307 divided by 30 rounds to eleven
14 APs, because fourteen physical ports remain free
10 APs, using 300 W of the remaining 307 W
questions.explanation: The phones reserve 63 W, leaving 307 W. Ten 30 W allocations fit, and there are enough ports; eleven require 330 W. This calculation uses the stated allocations rather than momentary measured consumption.

whyWrong.0: The problem explicitly supplies a 6.3 W reservation per phone.
whyWrong.1: Capacity must be rounded down; eleven allocations would exceed the remaining budget.
whyWrong.2: Available port count does not override the shared power limit.

exhibit.title: PoE allocation evidence — representative excerpt
exhibit.text:
Available: 370.0 W
Allocated: 345.0 W
Remaining:  25.0 W
Requested allocation on Gi1/0/13: 30.0 W
Operational state: power-deny

questions.prompt: A compatible AP requests 30 W of PSE allocation on a port whose configured maximum is 30 W. Its cable and hardware capability pass checks. What best explains the denial shown?
options: The 30 W per-port maximum is below the 30 W request
The known-good cable cannot carry the supported PoE allocation
The shared budget has only 25 W remaining for a 30 W request
The AP has no assigned IP address before power negotiation
questions.explanation: The per-port requirement is supported, but the shared remaining budget is insufficient. Provide supported capacity or move an endpoint to a compatible PSE with enough budget; verify actual requirements before changing limits.

whyWrong.0: The stated maximum equals the request; the shared allocation is the failing constraint.
whyWrong.1: The scenario verifies the cable and device compatibility.
whyWrong.3: PoE discovery and allocation do not require a preexisting host IP address.

questions.prompt: A virtual host presents tagged traffic for several VLANs over one physical uplink. Which connectivity choice fits that requirement?
options: A single access VLAN selected from the host’s management address
A voice-VLAN command for each of the virtual machines
An unconfigured port chosen only because its speed matches
A trunk with VLAN tagging and an allowed list matching the host
questions.explanation: Several tagged VLANs on one uplink call for compatible trunking at both ends. Chapter 10 teaches the configuration; a virtual host does not automatically imply LACP or a particular edge-protection policy.

whyWrong.0: One ordinary access VLAN does not carry all the stated tagged VLANs.
whyWrong.1: The voice feature is not a general list of VM VLANs.
whyWrong.2: Physical speed alone does not establish VLAN tagging and membership.

questions.prompt: An AP’s design uses one untagged management VLAN; client traffic is tunneled to its controller rather than locally presented as separate VLANs. Which port choice fits the stated uplink?
options: An access port in the AP management VLAN, with suitable power
A trunk whose native VLAN is chosen from a wireless client subnet
A voice port with the AP management VLAN used as voice VLAN
A routed port that removes the AP’s Layer 2 management VLAN
questions.explanation: Use the traffic actually presented by the AP. The stated tunneled design can use a single access VLAN; APs that locally present multiple VLANs require a different configuration.

whyWrong.1: The stated uplink presents only its untagged management network.
whyWrong.2: An AP management uplink does not require the phone voice-VLAN feature.
whyWrong.3: That changes the stated Layer 2 attachment rather than implementing it.

questions.prompt: Which endpoint calls for particular care before reusing assumptions from a single-PC access-port design?
options: A single printer specified to send one untagged data network
A single workstation with one untagged Ethernet interface
A standalone sensor specified to use one untagged data VLAN
A transparent firewall that bridges frames from other devices
questions.explanation: A bridging appliance can carry other devices’ source addresses and participate in a wider Layer 2 path. Review its forwarding role and VLAN requirements before selecting edge protections or MAC limits, which are taught later.

whyWrong.0: That stated requirement fits ordinary access-port selection.
whyWrong.1: That stated requirement fits the basic host-port example.
whyWrong.2: That stated requirement alone does not imply a bridging role.

questions.prompt: After erasing startup configuration on the referenced Catalyst platform, a technician still finds normal-range user VLANs. Which two statements explain how to verify this state? Choose two.
options: VLAN information can persist in the separate VLAN database
Erasing startup configuration guarantees deletion of every switch file
The name of a VLAN determines whether it is stored persistently
A remaining VLAN proves a router is still forwarding between subnets
Check VLAN definitions and interface assignments separately
questions.explanation: The VLAN database can persist independently of the startup configuration. VTP mode and platform influence how definitions are stored; inspect the actual VLAN database and running interface assignments instead of assuming a universal reset result.

whyWrong.1: Other persistent files can remain.
whyWrong.2: A VLAN label is not its persistence mechanism; inspect the platform's database and configuration.
whyWrong.3: A VLAN database entry says nothing by itself about routing.

questions.prompt: An untagged printer must join existing active VLAN 50 on unused Fa0/8. The port is enabled. Which interface configuration implements that requirement?
options: `switchport mode trunk` and `switchport trunk allowed vlan 50`
`switchport mode access` and `switchport voice vlan 50`
`switchport mode access` and `switchport access vlan 50`
`switchport mode access` and `switchport access vlan 1`
questions.explanation: Use static access mode and the required data VLAN. A voice-VLAN setting is a different operation; no multi-VLAN uplink is required.

whyWrong.0: A trunk is not the requested ordinary untagged endpoint attachment.
whyWrong.1: The voice command does not replace the printer's access-VLAN assignment.
whyWrong.3: This assigns a different VLAN from the requirement.

exhibit.title: Representative PoE configuration and state
exhibit.text:
Interface Gi1/0/7
 power inline never
Verified per-port capability: sufficient for this endpoint
Shared remaining allocation: sufficient
Observed endpoint power: off

questions.prompt: The compatible endpoint and cable work on a second PoE port. This port has sufficient supported power and shared budget. Which narrow change addresses the displayed administrative condition?
options: Set `power inline auto` on the intended supported interface
Assign the port to the endpoint's untagged data VLAN
Clear its dynamic MAC entries before retrying power
Add a management address to the switch's existing VLAN
questions.explanation: The port is administratively prevented from supplying PoE. Restore automatic detection on that port, then verify actual allocation and endpoint startup.

whyWrong.1: VLAN membership does not override the power administrative state.
whyWrong.2: Dynamic MAC state does not enable PoE detection.
whyWrong.3: A management IP address is not needed for PoE discovery.

questions.prompt: An ordinary PC must use a fixed access port in existing VLAN 10. The port operates as access but its administrative mode is dynamic auto. Which change completes the stated mode requirement?
options: Set `switchport voice vlan 10` and leave the administrative mode
Set `switchport mode trunk` while retaining VLAN 10
Set `switchport access vlan 10` again while retaining dynamic auto
Set `switchport mode access` while retaining access VLAN 10
questions.explanation: Operational access state does not mean the port is fixed in static access mode. Select the required administrative mode and verify both mode fields and VLAN membership.

whyWrong.0: Voice-VLAN configuration does not set static access mode.
whyWrong.1: A trunk does not meet the fixed access-port requirement.
whyWrong.2: The VLAN assignment is already correct; it does not change administrative mode.

questions.prompt: A replacement IoT sensor sends one untagged data network and needs PoE. Existing VLAN 60 is correct, but its static access port remains in VLAN 10 with power administratively disabled. Capability and budget are sufficient. Which two interface changes meet the requirement?
options: `switchport voice vlan 60`
`power inline never`
`switchport access vlan 60`
`switchport access vlan 10`
`power inline auto`
questions.explanation: Set data membership to VLAN 60 and enable supported automatic PoE detection. Those correct independent port attributes; the existing static access mode can remain.

whyWrong.0: The sensor requires a data access VLAN, not a phone voice VLAN.
whyWrong.1: This retains the power-disable condition.
whyWrong.3: This retains the wrong data VLAN.

exhibit.title: Supplied voice/data checks
exhibit.text:
Fa0/7 operational access VLAN 10, voice VLAN 30
VLANs 10 and 30 active
Phone power on; phone IPv4 address 0.0.0.0
PC data test to VLAN 10 peer succeeds

questions.prompt: The attached PC communicates normally. The powered phone's voice VLAN is active, but its displayed IPv4 address is 0.0.0.0; its design requires automatic addressing. What should be checked next before changing switchport mode?
options: Whether the working PC can still use its existing data-VLAN address
Whether the phone's required voice addressing and provisioning service is available
Whether changing both data and voice to VLAN 10 permits the phone to boot
Whether clearing the PC's MAC entry makes the switch assign the phone an IP
questions.explanation: Power and the switch-side VLAN assignment are verified, but the phone has not obtained its required address. Investigate the voice-network service and provisioning path; working PC traffic does not validate that separate service.

whyWrong.0: Repeating the working data test does not check voice address acquisition.
whyWrong.2: That discards the documented voice-network design without identifying the missing service.
whyWrong.3: The MAC table supplies forwarding locations, not endpoint IP configuration.

exhibit.title: Supplied endpoint and switch evidence
exhibit.text:
Documented LAN: VLAN 40, 192.168.40.0/24
PC-A: 192.168.40.10/24, no gateway, Fa0/1
PC-B: 192.168.41.20/24, no gateway, Fa0/2
Fa0/1 and Fa0/2: connected; static access VLAN 40
VLAN 40: active; fresh A and B MAC entries in VLAN 40

questions.prompt: Both PCs use the same active VLAN and their source MACs are learned on the expected ports. No router or gateway is configured. Which correction addresses the documented inconsistency?
options: Move PC-B's port to a new VLAN named after its current address
Give PC-B an unused address in the documented 192.168.40.0/24 LAN
Create a switch management SVI using PC-B's current address
Change only PC-A's mask to /16 while leaving PC-B at /24
questions.explanation: VLAN membership is correct, but PC-B's address belongs to another IP subnet. With no routing path, use an unused address in the intended LAN, such as 192.168.40.20/24.

whyWrong.0: Moving the port would break the documented common VLAN and would not supply routing.
whyWrong.2: A management address does not correct PC-B's local-versus-remote decision.
whyWrong.3: That makes the hosts disagree about on-link scope and does not implement the documented /24 LAN.

questions.prompt: An AP needs a supported 30 W allocation at the PSE. All listed PoE ports and cabling support its negotiation method. Which unused port meets both the per-port and shared-budget constraints?
options: SW-A: per-port maximum 15.4 W; shared remaining 60 W
SW-B: per-port maximum 30 W; shared remaining 25 W
SW-C: per-port maximum 30 W; shared remaining 40 W
SW-D: per-port maximum 20 W; shared remaining 80 W
questions.explanation: SW-C satisfies both constraints. Spare shared power cannot raise an individual port's supported limit, and an adequate per-port limit cannot create missing shared capacity.

whyWrong.0: The per-port maximum is below the required allocation.
whyWrong.1: The shared remaining capacity is less than 30 W.
whyWrong.3: The per-port maximum is below 30 W despite ample shared capacity.

cards.front: Do matching IP subnet settings put two ports in the same VLAN?
cards.back: No. Port membership determines the Layer 2 domain; host addressing does not change that membership.

cards.front: What are the normal and extended VLAN ranges on the lab Catalyst platform?
cards.back: Normal range: 1–1005. Extended range: 1006–4094. Usable user IDs also depend on reserved VLANs and platform support.

cards.front: Does default VLAN 1 imply secure management or static access mode?
cards.back: No. VLAN 1 is a default access/native VLAN, but port mode, IP management and authentication are separate configuration.

cards.front: Create VLAN 10 named USERS: commands and modes?
cards.back: At global configuration, enter `vlan 10`; at VLAN configuration, enter `name USERS`. The number identifies the VLAN; the name is a label.

cards.front: Two commands for a fixed access port in VLAN 10?
cards.back: `switchport mode access` and `switchport access vlan 10`. Verify operational mode and that VLAN 10 is active.

cards.front: Why inspect both the VLAN database and interface configuration?
cards.back: The database defines VLANs; interface configuration assigns ports. Normal-range VLAN data may persist separately from startup configuration, with VTP/platform-dependent storage behavior.

cards.front: What happens to a port’s data-VLAN assignment when that VLAN is deleted?
cards.back: The configured assignment remains, but the data VLAN becomes inactive. Recreate the VLAN or deliberately assign the port to the correct active VLAN.

cards.front: Access VLAN 10 plus voice VLAN 30: ordinary PC data and tagged voice?
cards.back: Untagged PC data enters VLAN 10; correctly provisioned phone voice tagged with 30 enters VLAN 30. The port can remain in access mode.

cards.front: How can a phone obtain voice-VLAN policy?
cards.back: Supported CDP or LLDP-MED discovery, or device provisioning/manual settings. Missing CDP alone does not prove every phone uses a particular fallback VLAN.

cards.front: Does successful PC traffic through a phone prove voice service works?
cards.back: No. Verify voice VLAN, power, provisioning and IP/call services separately. Switch-side voice configuration is not proof of a registered call endpoint.

cards.front: Does a missing data VLAN prove all traffic on a phone port must fail?
cards.back: No. A separate configured voice VLAN has its own forwarding context; investigate each traffic type and VLAN.

cards.front: Port-selection starting point for one untagged PC, printer or IoT network?
cards.back: A static access port in the intended VLAN. Add suitable PoE only when required; apply later security features after reviewing the endpoint’s behavior.

cards.front: AP with one untagged management VLAN versus several locally presented VLANs?
cards.back: The first can use an access port. Several VLANs presented on the uplink require compatible trunk tagging. Verify the AP’s actual forwarding design.

cards.front: What must be known before choosing a virtual-host uplink's VLAN mode?
cards.back: Which networks the host presents, and whether each is tagged or untagged. A virtual host does not automatically require a trunk or an LACP bundle.

cards.front: Why distinguish PSE power from PD power?
cards.back: The PSE supplies power; the PD receives it after cable losses. Compare a requirement with a rating measured at the same end.

cards.front: Can configuration add PoE capability to a non-PoE Ethernet port?
cards.back: No. The PSE hardware must support it. Then check per-port capability, PD requirements, cabling, administrative state and shared allocation.

cards.front: How do PoE automatic and never modes differ on a supporting port?
cards.back: `power inline auto` enables detection and allocation. `power inline never` prevents that port from supplying PoE; it does not choose the data VLAN.

cards.front: Which two limits must a new PoE allocation satisfy?
cards.back: The port must support it, and the switch must have sufficient shared available budget. Passing one check does not establish the other.

cards.front: What should you check after a power-denied indication?
cards.back: Requested allocation, remaining shared budget, configured per-port limit, device compatibility and cabling. Do not infer a unique cause from one status label.

tickets.title: Voice VLAN missing after a switch configuration change
tickets.scenario: A switchport is intended to provide data VLAN 10 and voice VLAN 30. The attached PC can still reach its same-VLAN peer. Phone power has been verified. You have the following switch evidence; no assumption about the phone’s fallback addressing is required.

exhibits.title: SW1 switchport excerpt
exhibits.text:
Name: Fa0/7
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 10 (USERS)
Voice VLAN: 30 (Inactive)

exhibits.title: Completed VLAN-presence check
exhibits.text: The complete VLAN database contains active user VLANs 10 and 20. VLAN 30 is absent; this is not merely an omitted line from an excerpt.

tickets.question: Which switch-side correction follows directly from this evidence?
options: Change the port's voice VLAN to the working data VLAN
Clear the MAC table without changing the VLAN database
Change the phone's address before restoring its intended VLAN
Restore the intended VLAN 30 in the VLAN database
tickets.explanation: The port references voice VLAN 30, but the VLAN is inactive and missing from the relevant database entries. Restore it, then verify port state and the phone’s separate provisioning and IP services. Data connectivity in VLAN 10 does not establish that voice works.
tickets.fix:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# vlan 30
SW1(config-vlan)# name VOICE
SW1(config-vlan)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/7 switchport
```
Confirm that voice VLAN 30 is active. Then check the phone’s actual VLAN settings and required IP/call services; the VLAN correction alone does not prove registration.

tickets.title: A workstation joins the wrong VLAN after a desk move
tickets.scenario: A workstation at 192.168.10.55/24 moves to a jack patched to SW1 Fa0/18. Its intended peers, including 192.168.10.60/24, remain in VLAN 10. The workstation cannot reach those peers. Its address and cable have been verified; no VLAN translation or alternate link connects the VLANs.

exhibits.title: SW1# show interfaces fa0/18 switchport — excerpt
exhibits.text:
Administrative Mode: static access
Operational Mode: static access
Access Mode VLAN: 20 (PRINTERS)

exhibits.title: Fresh source traffic learned on Fa0/18
exhibits.text:
Vlan  Mac Address     Type     Ports
20    0050.0f77.4a19   DYNAMIC  Fa0/18

tickets.question: What is the cause of the failed same-subnet communication?
options: The port is assigned to VLAN 20 instead of the required VLAN 10
The workstation's gateway must carry its same-subnet ARP requests
VLAN 20 is absent despite its reported active membership
The learned MAC entry is stale and still describes the old jack
tickets.explanation: The host addresses place the peers in the same IPv4 subnet, but the actual Layer 2 assignments separate them. The MAC-table entry confirms where fresh source traffic is learned. Restore the documented VLAN assignment and verify the local path. The entry was learned from fresh traffic on the new port, so clearing a supposedly stale record would not change its actual VLAN assignment.
tickets.fix:
```ios SW1
SW1# configure terminal
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/18
SW1(config-if)# description User workstation
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show interfaces fastethernet0/18 switchport
```
Generate fresh traffic, verify the MAC entry in VLAN 10, and retest the peer. Save the corrected configuration after verification.

chapters.title: 802.1Q trunks
chapters.subtitle: Carry several VLANs over one link, agree on tagging, and prove which VLANs can cross.

sources.title: Cisco: Catalyst 9300 IOS XE 17.12 — Configuring VLAN Trunks
Cisco: Configure 802.1Q Trunking Between Catalyst Switches
Cisco: InterSwitch Link and IEEE 802.1Q Frame Format
Cisco: Catalyst 3650 VLAN Command Reference — Native VLAN Tagging
Cisco: QoS in ACI — 802.1Q PCP, DEI and VID field definitions
