chapters.summary: Route between VLANs using a router trunk or a multilayer switch. Distinguish management addressing from packet forwarding, verify gateway prerequisites, and interpret SVI and subinterface failures.

sections.body:
A trunk extends several VLANs while keeping them separate. To send an IP packet from a host in one VLAN to a host in another, you need Layer 3 forwarding. You will build that function two ways: router subinterfaces sharing a trunk, and VLAN interfaces on a multilayer switch. The same addressing and packet-forwarding principles apply to both.

The examples use one IPv4 subnet per VLAN, which keeps host membership and routing boundaries clear. This is the design being taught, not a claim that an Ethernet VLAN can contain only one IP subnet. Complete routing-table selection and routes to remote networks come later; the first task is to make directly connected VLANs communicate reliably.

sections.title: Why a VLAN boundary needs a router
sections.body:
:::facts
- An ordinary switch trunk preserves VLANs; it does not route between them.
- A host sends an off-subnet packet to a reachable gateway in its own subnet.
- A router subinterface uses `encapsulation dot1Q vlan-id` to select its VLAN.
- An **SVI**, or switch virtual interface, gives a VLAN a logical Layer 3 interface.
- A multilayer switch needs `ip routing` to forward IPv4 packets between its connected interfaces.
- `ip default-gateway` supports a non-routing switch's own IP traffic; it does not enable inter-VLAN forwarding.
:::

PC-A is `192.168.10.11/24` and PC-B is `192.168.20.12/24`. PC-A calculates that PC-B is outside its local `192.168.10.0/24` subnet. It therefore sends the packet through gateway `192.168.10.1`. The gateway in this example also has `192.168.20.1/24` in VLAN 20, so it can forward directly to PC-B. PC-B needs its own correct gateway, `192.168.20.1`, to return the reply.

A common failed design has correct host addresses and VLANs but no routing device. Adding VLAN 20 to an allowed list will not fix that absence. Another has a working gateway but no gateway entered on a host. That host may communicate with local neighbors while failing to reach another subnet. Check the host's address, mask and gateway together; the mask determines when it uses that gateway.

**Router-on-a-stick** uses one physical router connection with several logical subinterfaces, normally one for each routed VLAN. A **multilayer switch** can perform the same routing through SVIs without sending every inter-VLAN packet over a separate router cable. Device features and performance depend on the model; choose an appropriate platform rather than assuming a product name guarantees routing capacity.

sections.title: Follow a packet through two VLANs
sections.body:
Use the packet walk from chapter 01 and add VLAN membership. Assume both ARP caches are initially empty, all ports are forwarding, and no NAT or filtering changes this simple exchange. PC-A first broadcasts an ARP request in VLAN 10 for `192.168.10.1`. The gateway replies with its VLAN 10 MAC address. PC-A can then send the ICMP echo request inside a frame addressed to that gateway.

At the router, the incoming Ethernet frame terminates. The router examines the destination IP and finds its connected VLAN 20 network. If it does not know PC-B's MAC address, it broadcasts a new ARP request in VLAN 20 for `192.168.20.12`. This is a separate broadcast: the router did not forward PC-A's VLAN 10 ARP into VLAN 20.

```diagram
{"type":"sequence","title":"Fig 11.1 — Resolve the next hop on each VLAN","caption":"Two separate ARP exchanges support one routed packet; the router then builds a new outgoing Ethernet frame.","actors":["PC-A · VLAN 10","Gateway · VLANs 10/20","PC-B · VLAN 20"],"steps":[{"from":0,"to":1,"label":"ARP: who has 192.168.10.1?","note":"Broadcast within VLAN 10"},{"from":1,"to":0,"label":"ARP reply: gateway MAC"},{"from":0,"to":1,"label":"Echo request for 192.168.20.12","note":"Frame destination = gateway's VLAN 10 MAC","accent":true},{"from":1,"to":2,"label":"ARP: who has 192.168.20.12?","note":"New broadcast within VLAN 20"},{"from":2,"to":1,"label":"ARP reply: PC-B MAC"},{"from":1,"to":2,"label":"Forward echo request","note":"New frame destination = PC-B MAC","accent":true}]}
```

The outgoing frame uses the router's VLAN 20 interface MAC as its source and PC-B's MAC as its destination. The source IP remains `192.168.10.11` and destination IP remains `192.168.20.12`. Ordinary routing does not rewrite those addresses. The IPv4 TTL decreases and the IPv4 header checksum is updated. The outgoing Ethernet FCS corresponds to the new frame.

| Point in the path | Ethernet destination | IP destination | VLAN |
|---|---|---|---|
| PC-A sends the echo request | Gateway's VLAN 10 MAC | `192.168.20.12` | 10 |
| Router sends the echo request onward | PC-B's MAC | `192.168.20.12` | 20 |
| PC-B sends the echo reply | Gateway's VLAN 20 MAC | `192.168.10.11` | 20 |
| Router sends the echo reply onward | PC-A's MAC | `192.168.10.11` | 10 |

With router-on-a-stick, the request travels toward the router tagged 10 and back toward the switch tagged 20 over the same physical link. With SVIs, the switch performs the Layer 3 transition internally. An endpoint's access link remains an ordinary untagged connection. Actual MAC values may be shared among logical interfaces on some platforms, so identify addresses from the device rather than expecting a different physical-looking MAC for every subinterface.

sections.title: Router-on-a-stick
sections.body:
Start with a switch whose PC ports belong to VLANs 10 and 20. Its router-facing Gi0/1 must be a static 802.1Q trunk allowing those VLANs. Configure native VLAN 99 consistently; it is unused for host traffic here. A router's ordinary Ethernet subinterfaces do not negotiate DTP with the switch, so dynamic auto is not a substitute for static trunk mode.

On a 2911 router, the following example uses Gi0/0 as the parent interface. Each subinterface receives the address that hosts in that VLAN will use as their default gateway.

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R1(config-if)# no ip address
R1(config-if)# no shutdown
R1(config-if)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.10
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 10
R1(config-subif)# ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 20
R1(config-subif)# ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.99
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 99 native
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# end
```

The suffix `.20` is a locally chosen subinterface number. It does not select VLAN 20 by itself; `encapsulation dot1Q 20` does that. Matching numbers make maintenance easier, but `Gi0/0.200` with `encapsulation dot1Q 20` would still identify VLAN 20. Configure encapsulation before the IP address so the router knows the VLAN interface's encapsulation.

In this design the parent interface has no IP address. Its operational state is still essential: shutting it down removes connectivity for every subinterface sharing it. An individual subinterface can also be shut down. Conversely, a subinterface can show up/up even when the far-end trunk omits its VLAN or its encapsulation identifies the wrong VLAN. Its state is not proof of end-to-end Layer 2 delivery.

The native subinterface explicitly represents untagged VLAN 99 and has no IP address because this example offers no VLAN 99 gateway. Tagged VLANs 10 and 20 are matched independently by their tags. Do not invent an IP address for every configured subinterface or assume every native VLAN must provide a routed service.

sections.title: SVIs on a multilayer switch
sections.body:
An SVI represents a VLAN rather than a physical socket. PC-A can attach to one access port in VLAN 10 and another VLAN 10 host to a different access port; both can use the same SVI address as their gateway. On the multilayer switch, create the VLAN, assign the access ports, and configure its SVI.

This excerpt assumes VLANs 10 and 20 and their access ports already exist:

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# ip routing
DSW1(config)# interface vlan 10
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface vlan 20
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show ip route
```

The logical interface and the VLAN database are different objects. `interface vlan 20` opens the SVI configuration; explicitly use `vlan 20` to create the Layer 2 VLAN. Then verify the state of both. A configured address cannot make an absent or nonforwarding VLAN usable.

With ordinary Catalyst SVI autostate behavior, three conditions are needed for the SVI to operate: the VLAN exists and is active, the SVI is not administratively shut down, and at least one eligible Layer 2 port in that VLAN is linked and spanning-tree forwarding. An access port can satisfy that last condition. A trunk can also satisfy it if it carries and forwards the VLAN. Advanced autostate exceptions exist, but the labs do not configure them.

These conditions explain why unplugging the only active host in VLAN 20 can take the SVI line protocol down. They also explain why unplugging one host might not do so when an active trunk still carries VLAN 20. Inspect all participating ports before drawing a conclusion from one disconnected cable.

An SVI can provide the switch's **own management address** without routing users between VLANs. On a non-routing access switch, an address such as `192.168.99.10/24` on Vlan99 makes the switch reachable in that subnet, provided the VLAN has a working path. `ip default-gateway 192.168.99.1` supplies a next hop for that switch's traffic to remote subnets. The remote network also needs a working path back; this command alone does not create it.

:::trap Reachable SVI does not prove forwarding
A host can ping its own SVI gateway address while the switch is not forwarding between VLANs. Check `ip routing` and the routing table. Once routing is enabled, the switch uses destination-matching routes instead of `ip default-gateway`. A default route is one possible route for otherwise unmatched destinations, not a requirement for communication between directly connected VLANs.
:::

sections.title: Routed ports and gateway designs
sections.body:
A **routed port** places Layer 3 addressing on a physical switch interface. On a supporting multilayer switch, `no switchport` converts the selected Layer 2 port to that role. Unlike an SVI, the routed interface is not associated with a switched VLAN or that VLAN's member ports.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/24
DSW1(config-if)# no switchport
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show interfaces gigabitethernet1/0/24 switchport
```

This example creates an ordinary untagged Layer 3 Ethernet connection to a router at `10.0.12.1/30`. It still uses Ethernet MAC addresses and ARP to reach that neighbor. “Routed” does not mean “no Layer 2 header”; it means the port is not participating as an access or trunk switchport. The displayed `Switchport: Disabled` confirms that role. Do not assume every switch model or interface supports conversion.

| Design | Gateway location | Physical connection | Main consideration |
|---|---|---|---|
| One router interface per VLAN | Physical router interfaces | Separate access link per VLAN | Simple separation but uses more ports |
| Router-on-a-stick | Router subinterfaces | Shared 802.1Q trunk | VLANs share the link's capacity and failure point |
| Multilayer switch with SVIs | Logical interfaces for local VLANs | Hosts use normal access ports | Routes between those VLANs internally |
| Routed switch port | Physical Layer 3 interface | IP link to a neighbor | Useful for connecting routing devices |

These designs can coexist. A distribution switch might use SVIs toward access VLANs and a routed port toward another router. The lab tests the routed port's directly connected neighbor only. Reaching networks beyond that neighbor requires appropriate forward and return routes, covered in the routing chapters. A successful ping between the two link addresses does not establish those remote routes.

sections.title: Verify and troubleshoot
sections.body:
Verify in layers. First inspect the host's IP address, mask and gateway. Then prove its access VLAN and local gateway reachability. For router-on-a-stick, inspect the switch trunk, router parent state, subinterface VLAN identifiers and gateway addresses. For SVIs, inspect VLAN existence, member-port forwarding, interface state and `ip routing`. Finally, verify a route to the destination and a return path.

The following is a representative, abbreviated modern IOS routing-table example for working VLANs 10 and 20. Older software may display connected entries without separate `L` entries.

```output R1# show ip route
C    192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10  ← Connected subnet
L    192.168.10.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.10  ← Router's own address
C    192.168.20.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20  ← Destination subnet for PC-B
L    192.168.20.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0.20  ← Router's own address
```

The `C` route represents the directly connected subnet. The `L` route represents delivery to the router's own address. Routes tied to an unusable interface are withdrawn; their presence therefore adds evidence beyond simply seeing an IP address in the running configuration. Their presence still does not prove that every endpoint has the right gateway or that the switch trunk delivers the correct tags.

| Evidence | What to investigate next |
|---|---|
| `administratively down` | The interface's `shutdown` setting and intended role |
| SVI protocol down without administrative shutdown | VLAN existence/activity and eligible forwarding member ports |
| Subinterface up/up, local gateway unreachable | Tag mapping, allowed list, access VLAN and host addressing |
| Every host reaches its own SVI but cross-VLAN traffic fails | `ip routing`, routes, addressing and any actual filtering |
| One-way or selective IP communication | Both hosts' masks/gateways and the return route |

Do not assign a unique cause to every up/down versus down/down combination across platforms. Those states narrow the search; `show vlan brief`, `show interfaces status` and the actual configuration establish the cause. Likewise, do not repair a missing VLAN by repeatedly applying `no shutdown` to an SVI that is already enabled.

sections.title: Exam focus
sections.body:
- Determine when a host uses its gateway and which MAC address it resolves.
- Follow the frame rewrite and separate ARP exchanges across a routed boundary.
- Configure router subinterfaces with correct tags, addresses and parent state.
- Create VLANs and SVIs separately and verify their operational prerequisites.
- Distinguish an SVI management address from enabled inter-VLAN forwarding.
- Use `no switchport` and interface addressing for a supported routed port.
- Interpret connected and local routes without treating them as endpoint proof.
- Diagnose from configuration, interface state and traffic tests together.

lab.title: Build two inter-VLAN gateway designs
devices: Part B: 1 × 3650 multilayer switch, 1 × 2911 router, 2 × PC-PT
Optional: 1 additional PC-PT for the challenge
lab.intro:
Practice revised September 2026. If you completed an earlier version, repeat the revised exercise and update its checkmarks.

Use two separate Packet Tracer files to compare router-on-a-stick with SVI routing. In each design you will verify the baseline, introduce one clearly defined fault, observe it, and restore it. The second file also includes a directly connected routed-port test.

Open device CLI tabs for console access. Answer `no` to an initial configuration dialog if offered. Interface names below match the selected Packet Tracer models; inspect yours before cabling. These instructions and representative outcomes were reviewed against Cisco documentation, but this exact lab has not been executed in Packet Tracer. Command support, output formatting and state transitions can vary by simulator release. A 2960 is used as a Layer 2 switch here; the SVI-routing portion specifically requires a multilayer model.

## Evidence to keep

For each design, keep the interface and VLAN/tag checks, both own-gateway tests and both inter-VLAN tests. For each fault, record the one change, the affected and unaffected checks, and the same checks after recovery. For the routed link, distinguish a successful neighbor test from evidence of a complete host-to-remote return path. A configuration screenshot alone does not establish forwarding.
lab.topology:
```diagram
{"type":"topology","title":"Lab 11A — Route two VLANs over one trunk","caption":"PC-A and PC-B use different subnets. R1 supplies both gateway addresses through Gi0/0 subinterfaces.","nodes":[{"id":"a","kind":"pc","label":"PC-A","sub":"192.168.10.11/24","x":1,"y":1},{"id":"b","kind":"pc","label":"PC-B","sub":"192.168.20.12/24","x":1,"y":5},{"id":"s","kind":"switch","label":"SW1 · 2960","x":5,"y":3},{"id":"r","kind":"router","label":"R1 · 2911","sub":"Gateways .10.1 and .20.1","x":10,"y":3}],"links":[{"from":"a","to":"s","toLabel":"Fa0/1","label":"VLAN 10"},{"from":"b","to":"s","toLabel":"Fa0/2","label":"VLAN 20"},{"from":"s","to":"r","fromLabel":"Gi0/1","toLabel":"Gi0/0","label":"trunk 10,20,99"}]}
```

| Part A device | Address / mask | Gateway | Cable and peer |
|---|---|---|---|
| PC-A FastEthernet0 | `192.168.10.11 / 255.255.255.0` | `192.168.10.1` | Straight-through to SW1 Fa0/1 |
| PC-B FastEthernet0 | `192.168.20.12 / 255.255.255.0` | `192.168.20.1` | Straight-through to SW1 Fa0/2 |
| R1 Gi0/0.10 | `192.168.10.1 / 255.255.255.0` | — | Parent Gi0/0 straight-through to SW1 Gi0/1 |
| R1 Gi0/0.20 | `192.168.20.1 / 255.255.255.0` | — | Same parent link |
| R1 Gi0/0.99 | No address; native VLAN 99 | — | Same parent link |

Only the physical Gi0/0 interface receives a cable. A subinterface is logical, not an additional socket. Leave PC DNS settings blank.

steps.title: Build Part A and configure the switch
steps.body:
Create a fresh file. Cable the four devices as listed and enter the PC settings through Desktop → IP Configuration → Static. Check each PC with `ipconfig` in its Command Prompt. Configure SW1:

```ios SW1
Switch> enable
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname SW1
SW1(config)# vlan 10
SW1(config-vlan)# name USERS10
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# vlan 20
SW1(config-vlan)# name USERS20
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# vlan 99
SW1(config-vlan)# name UNUSED-NATIVE
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if)# exit
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/2
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20
SW1(config-if)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if)# exit
SW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk native vlan 99
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20,99
SW1(config-if)# switchport nonegotiate
SW1(config-if)# no shutdown
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
SW1# show interfaces gigabitethernet0/1 switchport
```

:::expected
The PC ports belong to VLANs 10 and 20. Gi0/1 has the intended administrative trunk configuration. Its physical connection may remain down until R1 Gi0/0 is enabled in step 2. Hosts cannot reach gateways that have not yet been configured.
:::

steps.title: Configure R1's gateway subinterfaces
steps.body:
Enable the parent, then configure the two addressed subinterfaces and explicit unused native subinterface. The encapsulation command must identify the correct VLAN; matching the subinterface number is only a naming convention.

```ios R1
Router> enable
Router# configure terminal
Router(config)# hostname R1
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R1(config-if)# no ip address
R1(config-if)# no shutdown
R1(config-if)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.10
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 10
R1(config-subif)# ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 20
R1(config-subif)# ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.99
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 99 native
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# end
R1# show ip interface brief
R1# show ip route
```

:::expected
Once the link is operational, Gi0/0 and its enabled subinterfaces should be up/up. The parent and native subinterface remain unassigned, intentionally. R1 has connected routes for 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24. Modern IOS also shows local /32 routes for its own gateway addresses; do not diagnose an older simulator's lack of separate L entries as a fault.
:::

steps.title: Verify both local gateways and routed traffic
steps.body:
Before testing, write the destination MAC and destination IP you expect for PC-A's request before and after R1 routes it. Use role names such as R1's VLAN 10 MAC until you have observed actual values. Then test PC-A to its own gateway, PC-B to its own gateway, and both directions between PCs.

```text PC-A
ping 192.168.10.1
ping 192.168.20.12
```

```text PC-B
ping 192.168.20.1
ping 192.168.10.11
```

Allow spanning-tree startup and ARP resolution; repeat an initial partially successful test. Then collect:

```ios SW1
SW1# show interfaces trunk
SW1# show mac address-table
```

```ios R1
R1# show ip arp
R1# show ip route
```

:::expected
All four tests succeed after resolution. For the PC-A-to-PC-B request, the incoming destination MAC identifies R1 on VLAN 10 and the outgoing destination MAC identifies PC-B on VLAN 20. The destination IP remains 192.168.20.12; no NAT is configured. R1's ARP information associates PC-A with its VLAN 10 interface and PC-B with its VLAN 20 interface. In Packet Tracer Simulation mode, filter for ARP and ICMP and repeat a ping to inspect the addresses; cached ARP entries may mean no new ARP appears. Compare those fields with your prediction. If the simulator does not expose them, complete the same packet walk as a worksheet using the role names above, clearly marked as reasoned evidence rather than a captured packet. Save the file as `11A-router-stick-working.pkt` before introducing a fault.
:::

steps.title: Break one VLAN's tag mapping
steps.body:
Use File → Save As to create `11A-router-stick-experiment.pkt`. First predict which of the four tests will fail and whether up/up alone proves correct VLAN delivery. On R1 only, change subinterface .20 to expect tagged VLAN 200. Do not change SW1 or repair the router yet.

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 200
R1(config-subif)# end
R1# show ip interface brief
R1# show running-config
```

Repeat the gateway and cross-VLAN tests from step 3.

:::expected
PC-A can still reach 192.168.10.1, but PC-B cannot reach 192.168.20.1 and inter-VLAN traffic fails. The subinterface may remain up/up because the parent link is operational. The decisive mismatch is encapsulation VLAN 200 on R1 versus the client's VLAN 20 on SW1, not the .20 suffix. Record the running configuration and test results before recovery. If the selected image rejects changing encapsulation, record the rejection rather than claiming the intended fault was installed. Use the stated VLAN-200-versus-VLAN-20 mismatch as a supplied evidence exercise; do not report its predicted results as measured results.
:::

steps.title: Restore the correct encapsulation
steps.body:
Restore VLAN 20 on the affected subinterface.

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1Q 20
R1(config-subif)# end
R1# show running-config
R1# show ip route
```

:::expected
The encapsulation again matches VLAN 20. Repeat all four pings from step 3; they should succeed after any needed resolution. Confirm that VLAN 10 was not altered. The repair changes the actual VLAN mapping, not the subinterface's name.
:::

steps.title: Save Part A
steps.body:
Save each restored running configuration. Complete the destination prompt before moving to the other device.

```ios SW1
SW1# copy running-config startup-config
```

Press Enter at `Destination filename [startup-config]?` if offered and wait for completion.

```ios R1
R1# copy running-config startup-config
```

Complete the same prompt, then save the Packet Tracer file as `11A-router-stick-complete.pkt`.

:::expected
Part A is a separate, working file with correct tags and successful tests. Keep it closed or set aside while creating Part B; do not connect the two designs or reuse the configured router in the next topology.
:::

steps.title: Build Part B with SVIs but no forwarding
steps.body:
Create a **new** file containing a 3650 multilayer switch named DSW1, two fresh PCs, and a fresh 2911 router named R2. For now leave R2 uncabled. On a 3650 model that requires a power supply in the Physical tab, install the available compatible power supply and power it on before using the CLI.

| Part B device / port | Peer / port | Address / mask | Gateway |
|---|---|---|---|
| PC-A FastEthernet0 | DSW1 Gi1/0/1 | `192.168.10.11 / 255.255.255.0` | `192.168.10.1` |
| PC-B FastEthernet0 | DSW1 Gi1/0/2 | `192.168.20.12 / 255.255.255.0` | `192.168.20.1` |
| DSW1 Vlan10 | Logical VLAN 10 gateway | `192.168.10.1 / 255.255.255.0` | — |
| DSW1 Vlan20 | Logical VLAN 20 gateway | `192.168.20.1 / 255.255.255.0` | — |
| DSW1 Gi1/0/24, connected in step 11 | R2 Gi0/0 | `10.0.12.2 / 255.255.255.252` | — |
| R2 Gi0/0, connected in step 11 | DSW1 Gi1/0/24 | `10.0.12.1 / 255.255.255.252` | — |

Use straight-through cables from each PC to its switch port. Enter the PC addresses, masks and gateways. Explicitly disable IPv4 forwarding temporarily so the next step demonstrates what `ip routing` changes.

```ios DSW1
Switch> enable
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname DSW1
DSW1(config)# no ip routing
DSW1(config)# vlan 10
DSW1(config-vlan)# name USERS10
DSW1(config-vlan)# exit
DSW1(config)# vlan 20
DSW1(config-vlan)# name USERS20
DSW1(config-vlan)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/1
DSW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
DSW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/2
DSW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
DSW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface vlan 10
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.10.1 255.255.255.0
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface vlan 20
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show vlan brief
DSW1# show ip route
```

Predict whether the same four pings from step 3 will all pass before routing is enabled. Run those four commands in the new Part B PC windows and record local-gateway and cross-VLAN results separately.

:::expected
With both PC links up and forwarding, the two SVIs should be operational. Each PC should reach its own local SVI address. PC-A to PC-B must not be treated as a working routed service while IPv4 forwarding is disabled. This is the distinction being tested: assigning an IP address to the switch does not itself enable it to route user packets. Record actual model behavior if your simulator differs from the documented feature behavior.
:::

steps.title: Enable and verify SVI routing
steps.body:
Enable IPv4 routing, then repeat the own-gateway and cross-VLAN tests from step 3.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# ip routing
DSW1(config)# end
DSW1# show ip route
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show ip arp
```

:::expected
The two connected subnet routes are present and PC-A and PC-B communicate in both directions. No router trunk, static route or default route is needed between these directly connected VLANs. Save `11B-svi-working.pkt` as the working checkpoint. The uncabled R2 is not involved.
:::

steps.title: Remove VLAN 20's only active member link
steps.body:
Save a separate `11B-svi-experiment.pkt`. Before changing anything, predict the port state, SVI protocol state and connected-route entry. Then shut DSW1 Gi1/0/2, the only connected Layer 2 port in VLAN 20. Do not shut the SVI or delete the VLAN; isolating one change makes the observation useful.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/2
DSW1(config-if)# shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show interfaces status
DSW1# show vlan brief
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show ip route
```

:::expected
PC-B loses its link. Under normal SVI autostate behavior, Vlan20's line protocol goes down because there is no eligible forwarding member port, and its connected route is withdrawn. VLAN 20 still exists and the SVI is not administratively shut down. PC-A should still reach its own VLAN 10 gateway. Record actual status fields; do not insist that every image use the same up/down versus down/down wording.
:::

steps.title: Restore the access link and route
steps.body:
Re-enable the port, allow its startup forwarding transition, then recheck the SVI and routes.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/2
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show ip route
```

:::expected
Vlan20 becomes operational and its connected route returns once its member port is forwarding. Repeat PC-A to PC-B and the reverse ping. Both should work. Applying `no shutdown` to Vlan20 would not have fixed the physical member port that you actually shut down.
:::

steps.title: Add a routed connection to R2
steps.body:
Connect DSW1 Gi1/0/24 to fresh R2 Gi0/0 using a copper straight-through cable. Configure the two ends in separate CLI tabs. This step tests only those directly connected link addresses.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/24
DSW1(config-if)# description Routed-link-to-R2-Gi0/0
DSW1(config-if)# no switchport
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show interfaces gigabitethernet1/0/24 switchport
```

```ios R2
Router> enable
Router# configure terminal
Router(config)# hostname R2
R2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0
R2(config-if)# ip address 10.0.12.1 255.255.255.252
R2(config-if)# no shutdown
R2(config-if)# end
R2# ping 10.0.12.2
```

```ios DSW1
DSW1# ping 10.0.12.1
DSW1# show ip route
```

:::expected
The switch reports that Gi1/0/24 is not a switchport, and its table includes connected network 10.0.12.0/30. The two link-address pings succeed. R2 has no routes to the PC subnets in this exercise, so a PC-to-R2 ping is not an expected success test: R2 would need a return route. Do not add an unrelated default gateway command to DSW1 to conceal that missing routing design.
:::

steps.title: Save Part B and compare the designs
steps.body:
Save the restored configurations one device at a time.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# copy running-config startup-config
```

Press Enter at the destination filename prompt if offered and wait for completion.

```ios R2
R2# copy running-config startup-config
```

Complete that prompt and save `11B-svi-complete.pkt`. Write two short packet walks for PC-A to PC-B: one through R1's subinterfaces in Part A, the other through DSW1's SVIs in Part B.

:::expected
Both designs use the same host subnets and gateway addresses, and both route between VLANs. Part A sends tagged traffic over a router trunk; Part B makes the routing decision within DSW1. Part B's routed port is a separate Layer 3 connection, not the mechanism that joins its local VLANs.
:::

lab.troubleshooting:
- Own gateway fails on router-on-a-stick: check the PC mask/access VLAN, switch trunk, router parent state, subinterface tag and IP address.
- Subinterface is up/up but the gateway is unreachable: check tag mapping and delivery; up/up alone is insufficient.
- SVI protocol is down: verify the VLAN exists, the SVI is enabled and an eligible member port is linked and forwarding.
- Local SVI replies but cross-VLAN traffic fails: verify `ip routing`, both connected routes and both PC gateways.
- Routed-port neighbor ping fails: compare masks and addresses, check `no switchport` and administrative state at both ends.
- Some commands are absent in a simulator: record the exact model and limitation. Use the lesson's documented evidence for interpretation rather than treating a simulated omission as an IOS rule.
lab.challenge:
In a copy of Part B, add PC-C on unused DSW1 Gi1/0/3 using a straight-through cable. Create VLAN 30 and gateway `192.168.30.1/24`. Give PC-C `192.168.30.11/24` and that gateway. Prove that all three PCs communicate in both directions while the routed-port neighbor test still passes. Do not add a trunk or a default route. Before opening the answer, write the required VLAN, access-port, SVI and host changes yourself, and choose one verification for each. Re-test the existing VLANs as well as the new service.

:::solution Check your design
The new VLAN needs its Layer 2 membership, an operational SVI, and the correct host settings. IPv4 routing is already enabled from step 8.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# vlan 30
DSW1(config-vlan)# name USERS30
DSW1(config-vlan)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface gigabitethernet1/0/3
DSW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
DSW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 30
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# exit
DSW1(config)# interface vlan 30
DSW1(config-if)# ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0
DSW1(config-if)# no shutdown
DSW1(config-if)# end
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show ip route
```

Once PC-C's port forwards, Vlan30 is operational and 192.168.30.0/24 appears as connected. PC-C should ping 192.168.10.11 and 192.168.20.12, and both existing PCs should ping 192.168.30.11. DSW1 should still ping 10.0.12.1. R2 still lacks return routes to the PC subnets, so do not use PC-to-R2 success as this challenge's completion criterion.
:::

questions.prompt: With ordinary Catalyst SVI autostate behavior and the SVI administratively enabled, which two conditions are required for Vlan20 to operate? (Choose two.)
options: IPv4 routing is enabled globally.
VLAN 20 exists and is active locally.
At least one other switch is connected by a trunk.
An eligible Layer 2 port in VLAN 20 is linked and STP forwarding.
A default route points toward an external router.
questions.explanation: The VLAN must exist and have an eligible forwarding member link. Neither IPv4 forwarding nor an external route determines whether an ordinary management SVI can be operational.

whyWrong.0: An SVI can be operational for switch management while IPv4 routing is disabled.
whyWrong.2: A connected forwarding access port is sufficient; a trunk is not mandatory.
whyWrong.4: Default routing is unrelated to the local VLAN's SVI line-state prerequisites.

questions.prompt: Which two statements about ip default-gateway on a Cisco switch are correct? (Choose two.)
options: It supplies a host-style next hop while IP routing is disabled.
It installs an S* default route in the IPv4 routing table.
It supports the switch's own traffic toward other subnets.
It enables forwarding of user packets between SVIs.
It must be configured separately under every SVI.
questions.explanation: The command is a global host-style setting used when the switch is not routing. A switch with IP routing enabled uses its routing table instead; directly connected VLANs do not require a default route.

whyWrong.1: The host-mode gateway command is not a static routing-table entry.
whyWrong.3: Enabling user packet forwarding requires the relevant routing functionality.
whyWrong.4: The command is global, not a per-SVI configuration.

exhibit.text:
Port       Status       Vlan     Duplex  Speed

questions.prompt: What does the routed entry for Gi1/0/24 establish?
options: It is a Layer 3 physical interface rather than a VLAN switchport.
It is a trunk that carries every VLAN with an SVI.
It is an access port in VLAN 24 with a gateway.
It is a VLAN 1 port forwarding only management traffic.
questions.explanation: The port is operating as a routed interface, normally configured with no switchport on this platform. It can use Ethernet and ARP for its IP neighbor while remaining outside Layer 2 VLAN membership.

whyWrong.1: A trunk is a Layer 2 switchport and would be identified as a trunk.
whyWrong.2: An access port would show its VLAN membership.
whyWrong.3: A routed port does not become a management access port in VLAN 1.

questions.prompt: A host can ping its local management SVI. Which conclusion is justified by this test alone?
options: The switch routes all other connected VLANs.
The switch has a working default route.
Every trunk permits the host's VLAN.
The local host-to-SVI IP exchange works.
questions.explanation: A local SVI reply confirms that tested local exchange. It does not test forwarding between VLANs, remote routes or every trunk in the network.

whyWrong.0: A switch can answer at an SVI while IPv4 forwarding is disabled.
whyWrong.1: No remote next hop is needed for this local exchange.
whyWrong.2: The tested path need not cross every trunk.

questions.prompt: The router rejects an IP address on a new Ethernet subinterface because VLAN encapsulation has not been configured. The intended VLAN is 30. What should you do?
options: Enable the switch's VLAN 30 SVI and leave the router unchanged.
Assign the same IP address to the physical parent interface.
Enter encapsulation dot1Q 30, then re-enter the rejected address.
Rename the subinterface from .30 to .300 and repeat the address.
questions.explanation: Configure the subinterface's VLAN encapsulation before its address. An address command that was rejected is not queued for later application; enter it again after correcting the prerequisite.

whyWrong.0: This would change the gateway design rather than complete the router subinterface.
whyWrong.1: The intended service uses tagged VLAN 30 on a subinterface, not untagged parent addressing.
whyWrong.3: The suffix does not configure a VLAN association.

questions.prompt: R1 routes an echo request from PC-A (192.168.10.11) to PC-B (192.168.20.12), without NAT. What is in the outgoing Ethernet frame toward PC-B?
options: Source MAC R1's VLAN 20 interface; destination MAC PC-B; destination IP 192.168.20.12.
Source MAC PC-A; destination MAC PC-B; destination IP 192.168.20.12.
Source MAC R1's VLAN 20 interface; destination MAC PC-B; destination IP 192.168.20.1.
Source MAC PC-A; destination MAC R1's VLAN 10 interface; destination IP 192.168.20.12.
questions.explanation: R1 builds a new Ethernet frame for the outgoing VLAN. Ordinary routing keeps the packet's destination IP while changing the Layer 2 addressing for the next link.

whyWrong.1: PC-A's original Ethernet source is not retained across the routed boundary.
whyWrong.2: The destination IP remains PC-B's address, not R1's outgoing address.
whyWrong.3: This describes the incoming frame toward R1, not the outgoing one.

questions.prompt: VLAN 20 is active, Vlan20 is not shut down, and Gi1/0/2 is its only member port. What best explains the unusable SVI?
options: IPv4 forwarding is disabled globally.
VLAN 20 is missing from the VLAN database.
Vlan20 is administratively shut down.
Its only eligible Layer 2 member port is down.
questions.explanation: The supplied evidence shows no linked forwarding port in VLAN 20. Restore the intended member link, then allow forwarding convergence and verify the SVI and connected route.

whyWrong.0: Forwarding configuration does not supply the missing active Layer 2 member required by SVI autostate.
whyWrong.1: The display explicitly shows active VLAN 20.
whyWrong.2: The question establishes that the SVI is not shut down.

questions.prompt: A 2960 port toward a router-on-a-stick is explicitly dynamic auto. The router uses Ethernet subinterfaces and sends no DTP. What is the correct switch-side remedy?
options: Assign the router's gateway address to the switch's access port.
Configure a static trunk with the required VLANs and native treatment.
Enable dynamic auto on each router subinterface.
Set only the switchport trunk native VLAN, leaving the port in access mode.
questions.explanation: This peer will not negotiate the trunk. Configure the switch port explicitly as a trunk and match the subinterfaces' VLAN requirements.

whyWrong.0: A Layer 2 switchport address is not the missing trunk configuration.
whyWrong.2: The stated router subinterfaces do not provide DTP negotiation.
whyWrong.3: A native-VLAN setting does not make an access port operate as a trunk.

Host               Gateway           Last Use    Total Uses  Interface

questions.prompt: SW2 is intentionally operating without IP routing. Its management SVI is 192.168.99.10/24, and reachable router 192.168.99.1 has the necessary remote routes. Remote SSH packets arrive, but SW2 lacks a return next hop. Which command supplies it?
options: ip default-gateway 192.168.99.1
interface vlan 99 followed by shutdown
switchport trunk native vlan 99
questions.explanation: A non-routing switch uses ip default-gateway for its own traffic to remote subnets. The prompt establishes the other connectivity and routing prerequisites, isolating this missing host-style next hop.

whyWrong.1: A routing-table static default is not the host-mode gateway setting being used here.
whyWrong.2: Shutting the management interface would remove working local connectivity.
whyWrong.3: Native tagging does not supply a next hop for the switch's IP replies.

questions.prompt: On a supporting multilayer switch, which sequence converts Gi1/0/24 from Layer 2 to an enabled physical Layer 3 interface at 10.0.12.2/30?
options: interface vlan 24 → ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252 → no shutdown
interface gi1/0/24 → switchport mode trunk → ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252
interface gi1/0/24 → no switchport → ip address 10.0.12.2 255.255.255.252 → no shutdown
interface gi1/0/24 → switchport access vlan 24 → ip default-gateway 10.0.12.2
questions.explanation: No switchport changes the supported physical interface's role. It can then receive an IP address directly and be enabled with no shutdown.

whyWrong.0: That configures a logical SVI, not the physical port.
whyWrong.1: Trunk mode remains Layer 2 and is not converted by adding an address command.
whyWrong.3: Access membership and a host-mode gateway do not create a routed port.

exhibit.title: Representative excerpt — R1# show ip interface brief
exhibit.text:
GigabitEthernet0/0       unassigned      YES unset   up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0.10    192.168.10.1    YES manual  up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0.20    192.168.20.1    YES manual  administratively down down
GigabitEthernet0/1       unassigned      YES unset   administratively down down

questions.prompt: VLAN 10 works. The switch trunk carries VLANs 10 and 20, and R1's running configuration has correct encapsulation and addresses. Which change directly addresses the displayed VLAN 20 fault?
options: Add an IP address to the parent Gi0/0.
Enable unused Gi0/1 as a return interface.
Replace the VLAN 20 address with the VLAN 10 gateway.
Enter no shutdown under Gi0/0.20.
questions.explanation: The subinterface is explicitly administratively down. Enable that subinterface, then verify its connected route and VLAN 20 gateway reachability.

whyWrong.0: An unaddressed parent is intentional in this subinterface design.
whyWrong.1: The VLANs use Gi0/0; an unused physical port is not their return path.
whyWrong.2: The address is correct and changing it would introduce another fault.

questions.prompt: A switch must provide gateways for several local VLANs without sending all inter-VLAN traffic over a separate router trunk. Which design meets that requirement?
options: A router-on-a-stick with one shared trunk.
One access uplink with all hosts configured in different VLANs.
A Layer 2 trunk with every VLAN allowed.
SVIs on a multilayer switch with IPv4 routing enabled.
questions.explanation: SVIs can provide the local VLAN gateways while the multilayer switch routes internally. Actual forwarding capacity and supported features still depend on the selected platform.

whyWrong.0: This design explicitly depends on the separate shared router trunk.
whyWrong.1: An access uplink does not supply gateways for several VLANs.
whyWrong.2: A trunk extends VLANs but does not perform the required routing.

questions.prompt: Vlan30 is configured with an address and no shutdown, but is not operational. The complete local VLAN list does not contain VLAN 30, while the intended access port remains assigned to VLAN 30. What should be corrected first?
options: Apply no shutdown to Vlan30 again.
Create and activate VLAN 30 in the VLAN database.
Enable IP routing without restoring VLAN 30.
Change the host's gateway address.
questions.explanation: The missing VLAN database entry is established by the supplied evidence. Restore VLAN 30, then check that an eligible port is connected and forwarding; the SVI state alone would not uniquely prove this cause.

whyWrong.0: The SVI is already enabled; its missing Layer 2 VLAN is the established problem.
whyWrong.2: IPv4 forwarding cannot substitute for the absent VLAN database entry.
whyWrong.3: Host settings cannot create the switch's missing VLAN.

questions.prompt: SW1 sends ordinary native VLAN 99 traffic untagged to R1. Which subinterface command explicitly associates that untagged traffic with VLAN 99 on the router?
options: encapsulation dot1Q 99
switchport trunk native vlan 99
encapsulation dot1Q 99 native
switchport access vlan 99
questions.explanation: The native keyword selects the subinterface's handling of untagged native-VLAN traffic. Whether that VLAN also needs a gateway IP address depends on the design.

whyWrong.0: Without native, the subinterface identifies tagged VLAN 99 traffic.
whyWrong.1: This is a switchport command rather than a router subinterface command.
whyWrong.3: An access-port VLAN command does not configure router subinterface encapsulation.

questions.prompt: PC-A (192.168.10.11/24, gateway 192.168.10.1) starts a ping to 192.168.20.12. Its ARP cache is empty and no other traffic is involved. What is the destination MAC of its initial ARP request?
options: The broadcast address ffff.ffff.ffff.
PC-B's MAC, obtained from the remote destination IP.
The local switch port's burned-in MAC address.
The gateway's MAC, already inferred from its IP address.
questions.explanation: PC-A needs the local gateway's MAC for this off-subnet destination. It first broadcasts an ARP request within its VLAN; after the reply, it can send the echo request to the gateway's MAC.

whyWrong.1: An IP address does not reveal a remote Ethernet MAC.
whyWrong.2: Ordinary switching does not make the local switch port the IP next hop.
whyWrong.3: An empty ARP cache means the gateway's MAC must first be resolved.

exhibit.title: Representative DSW1 evidence
exhibit.text:
Vlan10   192.168.10.1   YES manual   up   up
Vlan20   192.168.20.1   YES manual   up   up

show ip route:
Default gateway is not set

questions.prompt: DSW1 has operational, correctly addressed SVIs for VLANs 10 and 20. Both hosts reach their own SVI, but the complete configuration contains no ip routing and the display is host mode. What is missing for forwarding between the two connected subnets?
options: A static default route toward the other SVI.
The global ip routing command.
An address on each Layer 2 access port.
Set ip default-gateway to the VLAN 10 host address.
questions.explanation: The switch has local IP interfaces but is not forwarding IPv4 between them. Enable IP routing, then verify the connected routes and host-to-host tests.

whyWrong.0: A default route does not replace enabling forwarding and is unnecessary between these connected VLANs.
whyWrong.2: The gateway addresses belong on the SVIs, not the access ports.
whyWrong.3: A host-mode next hop supports the switch's own remote traffic, not forwarding user traffic between SVIs.

questions.prompt: DSW1 routes connected VLANs 10 and 20 successfully. It has no default route. Which conclusion follows?
options: The VLAN traffic is being switched without a Layer 3 decision.
The hosts must use the routed uplink address as their gateway.
Connected routes are sufficient for those destinations; other destinations need matching routes.
The hosts must have a /16 mask to compensate for the missing default.
questions.explanation: Each destination subnet already has a connected route, so a default route is unnecessary for that exchange. A default or more specific route may be needed for other destinations, with a valid return path as well.

whyWrong.0: Cross-subnet communication still involves Layer 3 forwarding.
whyWrong.1: Each host uses a reachable gateway in its own subnet.
whyWrong.3: The existing correct subnet masks and connected routes support routing; widening host masks would make hosts try local resolution for remote destinations.

exhibit.title: Supplied link evidence after a cable move
exhibit.text:
Gi0/0       unassigned      down  down
Gi0/0.10    192.168.10.1    down  down
Gi0/0.20    192.168.20.1    down  down
Gi0/0 configuration: no shutdown; unchanged valid subinterface settings

questions.prompt: All subinterfaces use Gi0/0. What should be checked first, before editing each VLAN's encapsulation?
options: The physical Gi0/0 connection and its switch peer.
The IP mask on every host at the same time.
The native VLAN number on each access port.
A default route between the connected VLANs.
questions.explanation: The shared parent link is down, so each dependent subinterface lacks its physical transport. Inspect the parent cable and peer state, restore that link, and then recheck individual VLANs.

whyWrong.1: Changing correct host masks cannot restore the displayed router link.
whyWrong.2: Native settings concern trunk treatment and do not explain the physical link state shown.
whyWrong.3: A route cannot restore a down physical interface.

exhibit.title: Supplied complete relevant SVI state
exhibit.text:
VLAN 20 exists and is active; Vlan20 is enabled
All local VLAN 20 access ports: down
Gi1/0/24: operational Layer 2 trunk, link up
VLAN 20: allowed, active and forwarding on Gi1/0/24
No autostate overrides are configured

questions.prompt: Under normal autostate behavior, can Vlan20 remain operational with this state?
options: No; only a local access port counts toward SVI state.
Yes; an SVI stays operational whenever it has an IP address.
No; a VLAN needs both an access port and a trunk before its SVI works.
Yes; the forwarding trunk can provide an eligible VLAN 20 member.
questions.explanation: An eligible linked Layer 2 trunk can satisfy the member requirement for VLAN 20. The active VLAN and enabled SVI must also exist, as the question states.

whyWrong.0: An eligible access or trunk port can count.
whyWrong.1: An address alone does not satisfy the VLAN and forwarding-member conditions.
whyWrong.2: There is no universal requirement for both kinds simultaneously.

exhibit.title: Supplied host and switch checks
exhibit.text:
PC-B: 192.168.20.12/24; default gateway blank
PC-B pings local peer 192.168.20.13 and SVI 192.168.20.1
DSW1: ip routing; correct connected VLAN 10 and 20 routes
Other correctly configured hosts communicate between those VLANs

questions.prompt: PC-B cannot exchange traffic with remote VLAN 10 hosts. Which correction follows from the combined checks?
options: Replace PC-B's /24 mask with /16.
Assign the gateway address directly to PC-B.
Set PC-B's default gateway to 192.168.20.1.
Move PC-B into VLAN 10 without changing its address.
questions.explanation: PC-B's local path works, but it lacks a next hop for destinations outside its /24. Set the reachable local SVI as its gateway, then repeat remote tests in both directions.

whyWrong.0: A wider mask would make PC-B try local ARP for the remote VLAN instead of using its gateway.
whyWrong.1: The SVI already owns that address; assigning it to PC-B creates an address conflict.
whyWrong.3: Moving VLAN membership would break the documented addressing design.

questions.prompt: A Layer 2 access switch has no IP-forwarding capability. An available router has one Ethernet interface allocated to serve three VLANs. Which design meets those constraints?
options: Three gateway SVIs on the Layer 2-only switch.
A switch trunk to three addressed router subinterfaces.
One routed switch port per VLAN.
A single untagged router interface with no VLAN separation.
questions.explanation: Router-on-a-stick carries the separate VLANs over the one allocated Ethernet link. Each router subinterface supplies the correct VLAN mapping and gateway for its subnet.

whyWrong.0: Management SVIs do not give a Layer 2-only switch the missing routing capability.
whyWrong.2: The switch lacks routing capability, and the allocated router connection is singular.
whyWrong.3: One ordinary untagged interface does not provide the required separate VLAN mappings in this design.

whyWrong.3: The router's physical interface carries the subinterfaces and must retain this trunk design.

Check R2's return route to the host subnet.

whyWrong.0: The point-to-point routed link is already operational and reaches R2.
whyWrong.2: The host needs its reachable local SVI, not an off-subnet gateway.
whyWrong.3: A routed link's network number does not require a corresponding switch VLAN.

cards.front: When does a host use its default gateway?
cards.back: For a destination outside its local subnet, when the gateway is its selected next hop. It resolves the gateway's local MAC.

cards.front: What changes when an IPv4 packet is routed between two Ethernet VLANs?
cards.back: The router builds a new Ethernet frame and reduces TTL, updating the IPv4 checksum. Source and destination IPs remain unchanged in ordinary routing without NAT.

cards.front: Initial ARP destination when the gateway MAC is unknown?
cards.back: Broadcast ffff.ffff.ffff within the local VLAN, asking for the gateway's MAC. The later data frame uses the resolved gateway MAC.

cards.front: What is router-on-a-stick?
cards.back: Multiple VLAN gateway subinterfaces share one physical router link to a switch trunk.

cards.front: What binds Gi0/0.10 to VLAN 10?
cards.back: encapsulation dot1Q 10. The .10 suffix is a useful naming convention, not the VLAN binding.

cards.front: An address was rejected because subinterface encapsulation was missing. Next step?
cards.back: Configure the correct encapsulation, then enter the IP address again. A rejected command is not saved for later.

cards.front: How does a router subinterface explicitly handle untagged native VLAN 99?
cards.back: encapsulation dot1Q 99 native. Add an IP address only if that VLAN needs a routed service.

cards.front: Why statically trunk the switch port toward ordinary router subinterfaces?
cards.back: Those router subinterfaces do not negotiate DTP. Configure compatible trunk, allowed and native settings directly.

cards.front: Must the parent have an IP address in the lesson's router-on-a-stick design?
cards.back: No; its subinterfaces hold the gateway addresses. The parent must be enabled and physically operational.

cards.front: What is an SVI?
cards.back: A switch virtual interface represents a VLAN at Layer 3, providing switch management addressing or a gateway on a routing switch.

cards.front: What enables IPv4 forwarding between SVIs on a supporting switch?
cards.back: The global ip routing command. Operational SVIs alone do not prove that forwarding is enabled.

cards.front: Ordinary SVI autostate prerequisites?
cards.back: The VLAN exists and is active; the SVI is enabled; at least one eligible Layer 2 member is linked and STP forwarding.

cards.front: Does an SVI with line protocol down uniquely identify a missing VLAN?
cards.back: No. Check whether the VLAN is active, the SVI is enabled, and an eligible Layer 2 member is linked and forwarding.

cards.front: How do you convert a supported physical switch port to Layer 3?
cards.back: Use no switchport, assign the IP address and mask, and enable the interface with no shutdown.

cards.front: Does a routed Ethernet port still use MAC addresses and ARP?
cards.back: Yes. It has its own IP link but is not an access/trunk VLAN switchport. Verify Switchport: Disabled.

cards.front: ip default-gateway versus routing-table routes?
cards.back: The gateway setting supports a non-routing switch's own remote traffic. With IP routing enabled, destination-matching routes apply; a default route is not always needed.

cards.front: What do C and L represent in modern IOS routing output?
cards.back: C is a connected subnet; L is a local host route to the device's own address. Older images may omit separate IPv4 L entries.

cards.front: Where should an IP address go when a physical port is still a Layer 2 switchport?
cards.back: Use the appropriate SVI, or first convert a supported port with no switchport if a physical routed link is intended.

cards.front: Main connection trade-off: router-on-a-stick versus SVIs?
cards.back: Router-on-a-stick shares a separate router trunk across VLANs. SVIs route within a multilayer switch. Features and capacity depend on the platform.

cards.front: What does one physical router interface per VLAN require?
cards.back: A separate addressed router interface and an access link for each VLAN. It consumes more ports than a shared router trunk.

cards.front: Does a successful ping to a local SVI prove that the switch forwards between VLANs?
cards.back: No. Local IP reachability and forwarding between subnets are separate tests; a management SVI can reply while IP routing is disabled.

tickets.title: VLAN 30 loses its gateway after a cleanup
tickets.scenario: DSW1 is a 3650 multilayer switch with IPv4 routing enabled. It serves VLANs 10,20,30 through SVIs. PC-C is 192.168.30.11/24, gateway 192.168.30.1, on Gi1/0/5. After a VLAN cleanup, PC-C cannot reach its gateway. VLANs 10 and 20 still route successfully. Read the representative excerpts and the complete VLAN-presence check before deciding why Vlan30 is unavailable.

exhibits.title: DSW1 SVI configuration excerpt
exhibits.text:
interface Vlan30
 ip address 192.168.30.1 255.255.255.0
 no shutdown

exhibits.title: Completed VLAN and port checks
exhibits.text:
show vlan brief: VLANs 1,10,20 and the model's reserved VLANs appear; VLAN 30 is absent from the complete list.
Gi1/0/5 remains configured with switchport mode access and switchport access vlan 30.
Its switchport display identifies Access Mode VLAN: 30 (Inactive).

exhibits.title: Representative abbreviated IP interface display
exhibits.text:
Vlan10   192.168.10.1   YES manual   up     up
Vlan20   192.168.20.1   YES manual   up     up
Vlan30   192.168.30.1   YES manual   down   down

tickets.question: Which root cause is established by the evidence?
options: The Vlan30 SVI was administratively shut down.
VLAN 30 was removed from the local VLAN database.
PC-C uses an incorrect mask for its intended subnet.
IPv4 routing is disabled globally on DSW1.
tickets.explanation: The complete VLAN check proves that VLAN 30 is missing, while its SVI and access assignment remain configured. The SVI is enabled, the supplied host address and mask match the plan, and other VLANs still route. Its nonadministrative down state supports investigation but does not uniquely prove a cause by itself. Restore the missing VLAN and then verify forwarding membership; enabling routing or changing the host mask cannot replace that database entry.
tickets.fix:
Re-create VLAN 30 without changing the already-correct SVI address.

```ios DSW1
DSW1# configure terminal
DSW1(config)# vlan 30
DSW1(config-vlan)# name USERS30
DSW1(config-vlan)# end
DSW1# show vlan brief
DSW1# show interfaces status
DSW1# show ip interface brief
DSW1# show ip route
```

Confirm Gi1/0/5 is linked and forwarding in VLAN 30. Vlan30 should become operational and its connected route should return. Test PC-C to 192.168.30.1, then to a known host in another routed VLAN, and verify the reply path. Save after tests pass.

tickets.title: A new subinterface has no gateway configuration
tickets.scenario: R1 is a 2911 router-on-a-stick connected to SW1's static trunk. PC-C uses VLAN 30, address 192.168.30.11/24 and gateway 192.168.30.1. VLANs 10 and 20 work, but PC-C cannot reach its new gateway. The change record says a subinterface was added; the running configuration is the authoritative evidence of what actually exists.

exhibits.title: Representative excerpt — R1# show ip interface brief
exhibits.text:
GigabitEthernet0/0       unassigned      YES unset   up   up
GigabitEthernet0/0.10    192.168.10.1    YES manual  up   up
GigabitEthernet0/0.20    192.168.20.1    YES manual  up   up
GigabitEthernet0/0.30    unassigned      YES unset   up   up
