| R1 G0/0/0.10 | `10.220.10.1/24` | VLAN 10 `USERS`; DHCP pool for this subnet, exclude `.1–.49` |
| R1 G0/0/0.20 | `10.220.20.1/24` | VLAN 20 `STAFF`; ACL `NO-WEB-V20` inbound |
| R1 G0/0/1 — R2 G0/0/0 | `10.255.12.1/30` — `10.255.12.2/30` | OSPF process 1, area 0, router IDs `1.1.1.1` / `2.2.2.2` |
| R2 G0/0/1 | `10.220.30.1/24` | Server LAN |
| SRV | `10.220.30.10/24`, gateway `.1` | HTTP service on (Services tab) |
| PC-A | DHCP | Record the actual available lease within `.50–.254` |
| PC-B | `10.220.20.10/24`, gateway `.1` | Static |

Cables: PC-A → SW1 Fa0/1 and PC-B → SW1 Fa0/2 straight-through; SW1 Gi0/1 → R1 G0/0/0 straight-through; R1 G0/0/1 → R2 G0/0/0 **crossover**; R2 G0/0/1 → SRV **crossover** (or use the lightning-bolt auto-connect tool).


**Specification:** Create VLANs 10 USERS and 20 STAFF. Assign the two PC ports as listed with PortFast, sticky port security, maximum one secure MAC, and shutdown violation mode. Permit VLANs 10 and 20 on the router trunk, using native VLAN 1 at the switch and no untagged IP network at R1. R1 routes both tagged /24s and serves VLAN 10 DHCP, excluding .1–.49. Both routers run OSPF process 1, area 0, the stated unique router IDs, and passive LAN interfaces; keep the Ethernet transit at the default broadcast network type on both ends. Advertise both client networks and the server network. R1 accepts SSHv2 with a local user, with VTY source access restricted to 10.220.10.0/24. The inbound NO-WEB-V20 ACL on R1's VLAN 20 subinterface denies TCP destination port 80 from that subnet to SRV, and permits other IPv4 traffic. Do not enable Telnet or add unrelated routing/NAT features.

Use fresh devices. For this isolated project only, the reference account is `admin` with secret `Readiness-Lab-45` and domain `readiness.test`. Keep the console available. The named network SERVICES here is only an HTTP lab server; no DNS result is required.

steps.title: — Prepare the attempt
steps.body:
Place and cable the six devices from the tables. Set PC-B and SRV using Desktop → IP Configuration; enable Services → HTTP on SRV. Decline router setup dialogs. Save an untouched project as `readiness-start.pkt`, then Save As `readiness-attempt.pkt`. Write the intended addressing, policy direction and expected tests in your notebook. Start the timer only after cabling and the specification are clear. Do not read Steps 5–8 until the independent attempt is finished.

:::expected
The workspace and requirements are complete. Router links can remain down until their interfaces are enabled. You have not counted configuration performed while reading the reference as an independent result.
:::

steps.title: — Build from the specification
steps.body:
Work in an order you can verify: VLANs/access/trunk, gateway interfaces and DHCP, transit/server addressing, OSPF, SSH, then the HTTP ACL. Use IOS `?` if needed and record any external help. Name each device with `hostname`; icon labels alone do not change the CLI prompt. On PC-A select DHCP after R1 is ready and record its actual address. Stop the attempt at your chosen time limit, preserving unfinished work rather than copying the reference to improve the score.

:::expected
A completed build meets the written behavior; an incomplete build produces a precise list of remaining tasks. A lease can be any available candidate in 10.220.10.50–254. No score is earned merely for entering a command that was rejected.
:::

steps.title: — Test the behavior before reading the solution
steps.body:
Run these checks, taking notes about their limits:

| Check | Required observation |
|---|---|
| SW1 VLAN/trunk output | Correct access membership; Gi0/1 operationally carries VLANs 10 and 20 |
| Port security on both host ports | Sticky configuration, maximum 1, intended violation mode and learned client after traffic |
| PC-A configuration and R1 binding | Correct /24, gateway 10.220.10.1 and available lease |
| OSPF on both routers | FULL relationship; R2 learns both client /24s and R1 learns the server /24 |
| PC-A to SRV | Ping and numeric-address HTTP succeed |
| PC-B to SRV | Ping succeeds; a new HTTP request fails and matches the deny |
| R1 SSH from PC-A | Fresh authenticated SSHv2 session succeeds |
| R1 SSH from PC-B | Rejected by the VTY source restriction |
| Telnet from PC-A | Not accepted |

Use `show spanning-tree interface fastethernet0/1 detail` on SW1, plus its running configuration, to inspect PortFast; do not depend on an `Edge` text filter that may show nothing on this image. Compare current counters before and after new probes.

:::expected
Allowed controls and denied probes agree with the policy. A blocked web test alone could be a stopped server, bad route or filter; the allowed test and specific counter provide the missing context. A neighbor at FULL does not replace verification of the required routes.
:::

steps.title: — Record results and choose the revision task
steps.body:
Give one point per demonstrated check below, using your first-attempt state:

| # | Demonstrated result | # | Demonstrated result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Correct access VLAN on PC-A port | 9 | Transit addressed with /30 |
| 2 | Correct access VLAN on PC-B port | 10 | OSPF FULL on both routers |
| 3 | Required VLANs cross the trunk | 11 | Required routes in both directions |
| 4 | PortFast confirmed on both host ports | 12 | Host-facing OSPF interfaces passive |
| 5 | Port security configured and client learned | 13 | PC-A ping and HTTP succeed |
| 6 | Correct router subinterfaces up/up | 14 | PC-B ping works while HTTP is denied |
| 7 | DHCP pool/options/exclusions correct | 15 | USERS/PC-A SSH succeeds; STAFF/PC-B denied |
| 8 | Actual PC-A lease and gateway correct | 16 | Telnet not accepted on R1 |

Record elapsed time separately. Classify each miss as a concept, syntax, verification or platform-support issue. Compare with the reference only after preserving this record.

:::expected
The maximum is 16 local evidence points; it is not a Cisco score or a booking threshold. Unperformed and unsupported checks are marked as such, not passed. Select one concrete revision exercise for each missed skill.
:::

steps.title: — Compare the switch reference
steps.body:
The remaining reference steps are a learning review. Compare intent and evidence, not only line order. These blocks assume a fresh device or your compatible partial configuration; inspect differences before applying a line to an already configured port.

:::solution Switch reference — open after recording the attempt

```ios SW1
Switch> enable
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname SW1
SW1(config)# vlan 10
SW1(config-vlan)# name USERS
SW1(config-vlan)# vlan 20
SW1(config-vlan)# name STAFF
SW1(config-vlan)# exit
SW1(config)# interface fastethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 10
SW1(config-if)# spanning-tree portfast
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security maximum 1
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security violation shutdown
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security mac-address sticky
SW1(config-if)# interface fastethernet0/2
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 20
SW1(config-if)# spanning-tree portfast
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security maximum 1
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security violation shutdown
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security mac-address sticky
SW1(config-if)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
SW1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 10,20
SW1(config-if)# end
SW1# show vlan brief
SW1# show interfaces trunk
```

The access ports and trunk meet the specification. Sticky learning needs client traffic. If an old sticky address from a different host exists, investigate and remove only that lab entry before deliberately recovering the port; do not treat an unrelated violation as a network-address problem.
:::

steps.title: — Compare R1 gateways and DHCP
steps.body:
:::solution Gateway and DHCP reference
```ios R1
Router> enable
Router# configure terminal
Router(config)# hostname R1
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0
R1(config-if)# no shutdown
R1(config-if)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.10
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1q 10
R1(config-subif)# ip address 10.220.10.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# encapsulation dot1q 20
R1(config-subif)# ip address 10.220.20.1 255.255.255.0
R1(config-subif)# exit
R1(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 10.220.10.1 10.220.10.49
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool VLAN10
R1(dhcp-config)# network 10.220.10.0 255.255.255.0
R1(dhcp-config)# default-router 10.220.10.1
R1(dhcp-config)# end
R1# show ip interface brief
```

On PC-A select DHCP, then check `ipconfig /all` and R1's `show ip dhcp binding`. From each client ping its own gateway.

Both gateway subinterfaces have the correct tag/address and the parent is up. The pool permits 205 candidate addresses before leases/conflicts. Read the assigned address; no requirement forces .50 to be allocated first.
:::

steps.title: — Compare the routed path
steps.body:
:::solution Routing reference
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R1(config-if)# ip address 10.255.12.1 255.255.255.252
R1(config-if)# no shutdown
R1(config-if)# exit
R1(config)# router ospf 1
R1(config-router)# router-id 1.1.1.1
R1(config-router)# network 10.220.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
R1(config-router)# network 10.220.20.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
R1(config-router)# network 10.255.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
R1(config-router)# passive-interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.10
R1(config-router)# passive-interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.20
R1(config-router)# end
```

```ios R2
Router> enable
Router# configure terminal
Router(config)# hostname R2
R2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0
R2(config-if)# ip address 10.255.12.2 255.255.255.252
R2(config-if)# no shutdown
R2(config-if)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R2(config-if)# ip address 10.220.30.1 255.255.255.0
R2(config-if)# no shutdown
R2(config-if)# exit
R2(config)# router ospf 1
R2(config-router)# router-id 2.2.2.2
R2(config-router)# network 10.255.12.0 0.0.0.3 area 0
R2(config-router)# network 10.220.30.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
R2(config-router)# passive-interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R2(config-router)# end
R2# show ip ospf neighbor
R2# show ip route ospf
```

Run `show ip route` on both routers. From each client test the server before the ACL is applied.

The default broadcast network type is consistent at both ends. With two routers, the established adjacency can display FULL/DR or FULL/BDR according to the actual election; either can be correct. Costs depend on configured interface/reference bandwidth. R2 needs return routes to both client prefixes, and SRV needs its correct gateway.
:::

steps.title: — Compare SSH and the narrowly scoped HTTP policy
steps.body:
:::solution Management and HTTP policy reference
Configure the local SSH identity first:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip domain-name readiness.test
R1(config)# username admin privilege 15 secret Readiness-Lab-45
R1(config)# crypto key generate rsa
```

If prompted, enter **2048** for the modulus and wait. A release accepting `crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048` may use that equivalent. Keep an existing intended key rather than replacing it. Continue at global configuration:

```ios R1
R1(config)# ip ssh version 2
R1(config)# ip access-list standard MGMT-SOURCES
R1(config-std-nacl)# permit 10.220.10.0 0.0.0.255
R1(config-std-nacl)# exit
R1(config)# line vty 0 4
R1(config-line)# login local
R1(config-line)# transport input ssh
R1(config-line)# access-class MGMT-SOURCES in
R1(config-line)# exit
R1(config)# ip access-list extended NO-WEB-V20
R1(config-ext-nacl)# deny tcp 10.220.20.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.220.30.10 eq 80
R1(config-ext-nacl)# permit ip any any
R1(config-ext-nacl)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.20
R1(config-subif)# ip access-group NO-WEB-V20 in
R1(config-subif)# end
R1# show ip ssh
R1# show running-config
R1# show access-lists
```

Inspect `show line` and apply the same login/transport/access-class settings to any additional VTY lines the image exposes. From PC-A run `ssh -l admin 10.220.10.1`, authenticate, verify the prompt and exit; from PC-B try `ssh -l admin 10.220.20.1`. Repeat Step 3's application tests.

PC-A can manage R1 and PC-B cannot. The interface ACL blocks only the specified TCP destination service; it does not block ICMP, HTTPS or every application someone might call “web.” Do not claim broader isolation than the configured policy. This PT exercise verifies login behavior; real SSH server-key verification is taught in Chapter 29.
:::

steps.title: — Observe an incorrect DHCP gateway option
steps.body:
After the correct reference tests pass, save `readiness-verified.pkt`, then Save As `readiness-fault.pkt`. On R1 introduce one incorrect option:

Before making the change, predict whether PC-A will still reach an on-link address and whether its off-subnet HTTP request will work after renewal. Explain why an active DHCP binding could coexist with this fault.

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool VLAN10
R1(dhcp-config)# no default-router 10.220.10.1
R1(dhcp-config)# default-router 10.220.10.2
R1(dhcp-config)# end
```

Renew PC-A's lease by release/renew or its IP Configuration GUI. Inspect the resulting gateway before testing a ping to `10.220.10.1` and HTTP to SRV. Confirm no device uses .2. Do not repair until you have recorded the new host parameters.

:::expected
PC-A retains a valid subnet address but receives the wrong gateway. It can reach the real on-link gateway address directly, while off-subnet access fails in this design. The DHCP server can successfully lease a wrong option; a binding does not certify usable client configuration.
:::

steps.title: — Restore the correct option and retest
steps.body:
```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool VLAN10
R1(dhcp-config)# no default-router 10.220.10.2
R1(dhcp-config)# default-router 10.220.10.1
R1(dhcp-config)# end
```

Renew again and confirm the actual gateway is now .1. Repeat numeric HTTP, SSH and the PC-B restriction tests.

:::expected
Updating the pool is followed by a client option refresh. The original connectivity returns without changing OSPF or relaxing the ACL. The deliberately wrong .2 is inside the excluded DHCP range and is unassigned in this fresh topology.
:::

steps.title: — Save the result and schedule a changed attempt
steps.body:
On SW1, R1 and R2, issue `copy running-config startup-config` one device at a time and accept its destination prompt. Save `readiness-repaired.pkt`. Keep the first-attempt score and later corrected result separate. Make the next attempt in a fresh project after a delay, using the changed challenge below. Do not erase the only verified copy.

:::expected
Your record shows the original gaps, the observed fault and the verified recovery. Successful completion covers this bounded topology; record independent evidence for the wireless, IPv6, automation and other objectives it omits.
:::

Reconcile the result with your selected blueprint. This build does not assess IPv6 routing/OSPFv3, EtherChannel failover, wireless GUI/security, DNS diagnosis, NAT, VPN interpretation, secure file transfer, device AAA server integration or automation/AI decisions. NTP, syslog, SNMP and QoS also need their own evidence where your track calls for them. Use the relevant earlier labs and the mixed checkpoint to find gaps; do not extrapolate these 16 local checks into whole-exam readiness.

lab.troubleshooting:
- A 169.254 address or missing binding calls for tracing DHCP messages, VLAN reachability, pool capacity/options, relay requirements and filtering; it does not identify one cause by itself.
- No OSPF neighbor calls for both-side interface, subnet, area, timer and passive checks. A broader network wildcard is not inherently wrong if it enables the intended interface.
- EXSTART/EXCHANGE can result from an MTU problem, but verify advertised/configured values and the actual path before changing them. Do not apply mtu-ignore as a routine repair.
- A failed HTTP page with successful ping requires service and TCP/policy checks. Correlate the correct ACL line with a fresh request.
- A port-security violation can result from a different learned client. Inspect the exact secure entry before clearing or restarting anything.
lab.challenge:
Build a fresh variation with VLAN 30 as USERS (`172.20.30.0/24`) and VLAN 40 as STAFF (`172.20.40.0/24`). Keep the transit and server network unchanged. Give USERS DHCP .50–.254, restrict R1 SSH to USERS, and now deny **ICMP echo requests** from STAFF to SRV while allowing its HTTP. Write the expected opposite results for ping and HTTP before building.

:::solution Compare the changed attempt after testing
Update switch VLANs/access assignments/trunk allowance, R1 subinterface tags and addresses, DHCP pool/exclusions/options, both advertised client networks, and MGMT-SOURCES. Replace the HTTP deny with `deny icmp 172.20.40.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.220.30.10 echo`, followed by `permit ip any any`, attached inbound on the VLAN 40 subinterface. STAFF ping fails while its new HTTP request succeeds; USERS can reach SRV and manage R1. The changed protocols and directions must be verified, not inferred from the earlier score.

The fresh-project policy can use this complete list and attachment:

```ios R1
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip access-list extended STAFF-IN
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 10 deny icmp 172.20.40.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.220.30.10 echo
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 20 permit ip any any
R1(config-ext-nacl)# exit
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.40
R1(config-subif)# ip access-group STAFF-IN in
R1(config-subif)# end
R1# show ip interface gigabitethernet0/0/0.40
R1# show access-lists STAFF-IN
```

Use the new client addresses for all probes. Record both route directions, the actual DHCP options, a successful USERS SSH login, a denied STAFF login, STAFF HTTP success and its echo-request denial. If a test fails, preserve the evidence before comparing configuration. An unused old ACL name is not proof the correct list is attached to the new interface.
:::

questions.prompt: Two routers use OSPFv2 on the same broadcast subnet. Among these choices, which two interface parameters must agree for normal neighbor formation? (Choose two.)
options: Local OSPF process ID
Hello and dead intervals
OSPF router ID
OSPF area ID
Configured interface bandwidth
questions.explanation: The hello/dead intervals and area must match in this scenario. This is not a complete checklist: subnet, enabled protocol, authentication where used and other compatibility settings also matter.

whyWrong.0: Process ID is locally significant.
whyWrong.2: Router IDs should be unique rather than identical.
whyWrong.4: Different bandwidth values can affect costs without preventing hello compatibility.

exhibit.title: Representative Cisco syslog content
exhibit.text:
%LINK-3-UPDOWN: Interface Gi0/1, changed state to down
%LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Gi0/1, changed state to down

questions.prompt: What do the 3 and 5 identify in these Cisco message headers?
options: Transport facility numbers assigned to the two receivers
Severity codes for critical and warning messages respectively
Severity codes for error and notification messages respectively
Sequence numbers used to reorder the messages at the server
questions.explanation: The numeric field between the Cisco component and mnemonic is severity: 3 is error and 5 is notification. LINK and LINEPROTO are Cisco message components, often called facilities in IOS documentation; they are not the numeric transport PRI facility.

whyWrong.0: The transport facility is encoded separately in PRI when that transport format is used.
whyWrong.1: Critical is 2 and warning is 4.
whyWrong.3: These numeric fields are severity, not optional message sequence numbers.

questions.prompt: On the documented Catalyst IOS static access-port implementation, port security is newly enabled and no optional values are changed. Which two defaults apply? (Choose two.)
options: Sticky learning is automatically enabled
Maximum secure MAC addresses is one
The switchport remains dynamic auto
Violation mode is restrict without shutdown
Violation mode is shutdown
questions.explanation: For this scoped implementation, the default maximum is one and the default violation action is shutdown. Verify the actual port state and configuration rather than treating every switching platform as identical.

whyWrong.0: Sticky learning requires its own command.
whyWrong.2: Port security requires a supported static switchport mode.
whyWrong.3: Restrict is an explicitly selected alternative.

exhibit.title: Representative HTTP response body
exhibit.text: {"hostname":"SW1","uptime":86400,"managed":true,"interfaces":[{"name":"Gi0/1","status":"up"},{"name":"Gi0/2","status":"down"}]}

questions.prompt: Which description correctly identifies the interfaces value in the displayed JSON?
options: An object containing two unquoted member names
A string containing two comma-separated interface values
A Boolean value because each status is either up or down
An array whose elements are two interface objects
questions.explanation: The outer square brackets identify an array, and each pair of braces encloses an object. The strings up/down are not JSON Booleans; the unquoted true value is Boolean.

whyWrong.0: The interfaces value starts with brackets rather than an object brace.
whyWrong.1: It is structured JSON, not a quoted string.
whyWrong.2: The status members are strings, and the interfaces value is an array.

questions.prompt: For Cisco IOS management AAA, which conventional protocol/transport supports the standard per-command authorization design?
options: Classic RADIUS over UDP 1812
TACACS+ over TCP 49
Classic RADIUS accounting over UDP 1813
TACACS+ over UDP 49
questions.explanation: TACACS+ over TCP 49 supports separate authentication, authorization and accounting exchanges, including IOS command authorization. Classic TACACS+ body protection is shared-secret obfuscation and is not equivalent to modern TLS channel security.

whyWrong.0: This RADIUS authentication service is not the standard IOS TACACS+ per-command authorization mechanism.
whyWrong.2: The accounting port records events rather than authorizing each command in this design.
whyWrong.3: TACACS+ uses TCP for the conventional service.

questions.prompt: SW1 uses LACP passive on otherwise compatible member ports. Which SW2 mode initiates the protocol needed to form that bundle?
options: passive
desirable
active
auto
questions.explanation: LACP active initiates and passive responds. Desirable and auto belong to PAgP, not an automatic choice between channel protocols.

whyWrong.0: Two passive ends lack an initiator.
whyWrong.1: Desirable initiates PAgP rather than LACP.
whyWrong.3: Auto is a PAgP mode and does not answer LACP.

questions.prompt: This ordinary Ethernet host uses no special on-link route or proxy arrangement. Its intended gateway is on its local subnet. Which displayed setting is inconsistent?
options: The host address is the subnet broadcast address
The configured gateway lies outside the host’s /22
The subnet mask must be /16 because the address begins 172.16
The host and gateway have the same IPv4 address
questions.explanation: 172.16.47.250/22 belongs to 172.16.44.0–172.16.47.255; usable hosts end at .47.254. The configured gateway is outside that range, so it is unsuitable for the stated ordinary local-gateway design.

whyWrong.0: The broadcast address is 172.16.47.255, not .250.
whyWrong.2: Classful assumptions do not override the configured CIDR mask.
whyWrong.3: The displayed host and gateway addresses differ.

spec.title: VLAN 10 · Rapid PVST+
spec.caption: SW1 is root; the labeled short-method costs are authoritative for this calculation.

questions.prompt: SW1 is the root. Using the explicitly shown path costs, which SW3 interface becomes the root port?
options: Fa0/24, because one hop always beats two
Gi0/1, because SW2’s MAC overrides root cost
Gi0/1, because the path through SW2 costs 8
Fa0/24, because its displayed number is lower
questions.explanation: SW3 adds its receiving-interface cost 4 to SW2’s advertised root cost 4, for a total of 8. The direct link costs 19, so no equal-cost tie-breaker is needed.

whyWrong.0: Hop count is not the STP path metric.
whyWrong.1: Sender bridge ID matters only after the earlier cost comparison.
whyWrong.3: The unequal costs decide before port-ID tie-breakers.

questions.prompt: Under ordinary destination-based forwarding, which next hop is selected for 10.1.3.77 from these installed routes?
options: 10.9.9.2 because the static route has lower AD
10.9.9.1 because its OSPF metric is lower
203.0.113.1 because it is the default gateway
10.9.9.3 because the matching /26 is longest
questions.explanation: 10.1.3.77 is in 10.1.3.64/26, the most-specific matching installed route. AD does not let the less-specific /24 override it.

whyWrong.0: AD compares competing route sources for the same prefix.
whyWrong.1: The /16 is less specific despite its lower metric.
whyWrong.2: The default is used when no more-specific installed route matches.

exhibit.title: Representative R1 NAT configuration
exhibit.text:
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/0
 ip address 10.10.10.1 255.255.255.0
 ip nat inside
interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1
 ip address 203.0.113.2 255.255.255.252
ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/0/1 overload
access-list 1 permit 10.10.10.0 0.0.0.255

questions.prompt: Eligible client packets enter Gi0/0/0 and leave Gi0/0/1 in this conventional inside-source PAT design. Routes and filtering are correct. Which missing interface setting prevents the shown mapping from operating as intended?
options: ip nat outside on GigabitEthernet0/0/1
ip nat outside on GigabitEthernet0/0/0
A permit for 203.0.113.0/30 in source ACL 1
A pool statement replacing interface overload
questions.explanation: The intended egress lacks its outside designation. Correct that demonstrated omission and verify fresh traffic; an empty translation table by itself could have several causes.

whyWrong.1: The client-facing interface is the intended inside interface.
whyWrong.2: The source ACL selects client addresses to translate, not the resulting outside address.
whyWrong.3: Interface overload is a valid PAT form and does not require a named pool.

questions.prompt: Build numbered ACL 110 to deny Telnet from 192.168.10.0/24 to 10.0.0.5 and permit all other IPv4 packets. Which two entries are needed, with the deny entered first? (Choose two.)
options: access-list 110 permit ip any any
access-list 110 permit tcp any any eq 23
questions.explanation: The extended deny matches the source /24, destination host and TCP destination port 23. A subsequent general IPv4 permit avoids unintentionally denying all other traffic; interface attachment must still match the intended path.

whyWrong.1: That wildcard ignores the first three octets and fixes the last octet at zero.
whyWrong.3: Deny ip would also block other services from that source to the host.
whyWrong.4: Permitting only Telnet leaves other protocols subject to the implicit deny.

questions.prompt: The remote DHCP server 10.0.0.10 has the correct VLAN 20 pool and a working return route. Client broadcasts arrive at R1 Gi0/0.20, but that interface has no relay configuration. Which addition fits?
options: ip helper-address 10.0.0.10 on Gi0/0.20
ip helper-address 10.0.0.10 on the server-facing interface
default-router 10.0.0.10 in a new local DHCP pool
ip address 10.0.0.10 on the VLAN 20 subinterface
questions.explanation: The helper is placed on the interface receiving client broadcasts. It relays toward the named server and supplies relay information used for pool selection; the prompt establishes the other prerequisites.

whyWrong.1: That interface does not receive the original client broadcast.
whyWrong.2: A new local pool changes the intended remote-server design.
whyWrong.3: Assigning the server’s address to the router creates a different addressing fault.

exhibit.title: Representative R2 HSRP brief
exhibit.text:
P indicates configured to preempt
Interface Grp Pri P State    Active     Standby Virtual IP
Gi0/0     1   150   Standby 10.1.1.1   local   10.1.1.254

questions.prompt: R1 became active before R2 joined and remains healthy at priority 100. R2 now shows priority 150 without a P flag. What explains its standby role?
options: The lower IP address must remain active in every HSRP group
Priority 150 is outside the supported HSRP range
R1’s router ID overrides the HSRP priority comparison
R2 has not been configured to preempt the existing active router
questions.explanation: A higher-priority HSRP router does not take over a healthy existing active router solely by joining when preemption is disabled. The missing P flag supports that explanation; configured preemption delays and actual status should also be inspected before changing roles.

whyWrong.0: The active role is not universally assigned to the lower IP address.
whyWrong.1: 150 is a valid priority.
whyWrong.2: An OSPF router ID does not control HSRP roles.

questions.prompt: Three nearby US-domain 2.4 GHz APs use 20 MHz channels 1,4,8. A survey confirms adjacent-channel overlap. Which plan reduces that overlap while retaining three 20 MHz cells?
options: Put all three APs on channel 6 at maximum power
Use channels 1,6,11 with survey-appropriate power
Change the middle AP to a bonded 40 MHz channel
Keep channels 1,4,8 and increase all transmit powers
questions.explanation: 1,6,11 is the conventional separated 2.4 GHz channel plan for this setting. The survey and local rules still govern reuse, power and interference; channel numbers alone do not guarantee throughput.

whyWrong.0: Co-channel reuse requires shared airtime and does not provide three separate channels.
whyWrong.2: A wider channel consumes more of this limited band.
whyWrong.3: Increasing power does not remove frequency overlap and can increase the affected area.

questions.prompt: For this exercise, construct an IPv6 link-local address with first 64 bits FE80:0:0:0 and a modified EUI-64 IID from 00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E. Which result is correct?
options: FE80::21A:2BFF:FE3C:4D5E
FE80::1A:2BFF:FE3C:4D5E
FE80::1A2B:3CFF:FE4D:5E00
questions.explanation: Insert FF:FE between the MAC halves and invert the first octet’s U/L bit with XOR 0x02. The IID is 021A:2BFF:FE3C:4D5E; leading-zero compression gives the first choice.

whyWrong.1: This leaves the U/L bit unchanged.
whyWrong.2: This omits FF:FE and does not construct the intended 64-bit IID.
whyWrong.3: This rearranges the MAC bytes incorrectly.

exhibit.title: Representative authoritative answer and change record
exhibit.text:
portal.example.test. 300 IN A 192.0.2.15
Approved new web address: 192.0.2.25
HTTP to 192.0.2.25: expected page

questions.prompt: The authoritative DNS answer for portal.example.test is shown. The change record says the web server moved to 192.0.2.25 and the new address serves the expected page. Which record needs correction?
options: The MX record naming the mail exchanger
The PTR record used only for reverse lookup
The NS record naming the authoritative servers
The A record still pointing at the previous IPv4 address
questions.explanation: The A record supplies the IPv4 address used for this forward lookup. Correct the authoritative data and assess caching/TTL before concluding every client has received the new answer.

whyWrong.0: Mail exchange is not the requested web hostname’s IPv4 mapping.
whyWrong.1: A reverse record does not replace the forward A record used here.
whyWrong.2: The evidence identifies an answer-data problem rather than an incorrect delegation.

questions.prompt: A play targets IOS devices with a working network_cli connection. Which task choice gathers the current IPv4 routing table without intentionally changing configuration?
options: cisco.ios.ios_command with commands: [show ip route]
cisco.ios.ios_config with lines: [ip routing]
ansible.builtin.shell with commands: [show ip route]
cisco.ios.ios_config with lines: [no ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0]
questions.explanation: ios_command executes supported operational commands through the network connection. Verify the inventory target, authentication and returned device output; the name of a module alone does not guarantee every possible command is read-only.

whyWrong.1: This requests a configuration change.
whyWrong.2: shell is not the matching IOS network_cli command module, and commands is not its shown interface.
whyWrong.3: This asks to remove routing configuration.

questions.prompt: An approved assistant will receive sanitized lab evidence. The review must compare possible DHCP causes and return a table of read-only checks, without making changes. Which prompt meets that contract?
options: Act as a network analyst. Use this sanitized evidence to choose the most likely relay repair and return its configuration commands.
Act as a network analyst. Treat these sanitized exhibits as lab data; return a table of facts, competing causes and read-only checks with reasons. Do not make changes.
Act as a network analyst. Use these sanitized exhibits to write a chronological incident summary with no proposed tests.
Act as a network analyst. Treat these sanitized exhibits as lab data; assume the pool is exhausted and return read-only checks of that cause only.
questions.explanation: The prompt specifies a useful role, approved data, task boundary and output format while preserving uncertainty. Its recommendations still need verification against the actual devices and documentation.

whyWrong.0: The request needs comparative diagnosis and read-only checks, not a preselected repair configuration.
whyWrong.2: A summary omits the requested competing causes and diagnostic checks.
whyWrong.3: The requested comparison cannot be met by assuming one cause before testing it.

questions.prompt: R1 learns the neighbor link-local address FE80::2 on Gi0/0/1. Which IPv6 static-route form identifies the correct link for destination 2001:DB8:20::/64?
options: ip route 2001:DB8:20::/64 gigabitethernet0/0/1 FE80::2
ipv6 route 2001:DB8:20::/64 gigabitethernet0/0/1 FE80::2
ipv6 route FE80::/64 gigabitethernet0/0/1 2001:DB8:20::2
questions.explanation: A link-local next hop needs an outgoing interface because the same address scope can exist on different links. Verify next-hop reachability, route installation and the destination’s return route after configuration.

whyWrong.0: The interface is missing for this link-local next hop.
whyWrong.1: ip route is the IPv4 command family.
whyWrong.3: This changes the destination prefix and next-hop roles.

questions.prompt: A lab host runs two VMs with different guest operating systems and several containers on one Linux VM. Which description correctly locates their kernels?
options: Each VM has a guest kernel; those Linux containers share their container host’s kernel
All VMs and containers on the hardware must share one guest kernel
Each container needs a complete independent guest kernel just like a VM
The switch chooses a kernel according to the container VLAN tag
questions.explanation: A VM provides a guest operating-system environment with its own kernel. Ordinary OS-level containers share their host kernel while isolating processes and resources. Here their host is the Linux VM.

whyWrong.1: The hypervisor can host separate guest kernels; a VM is not merely another host process namespace.
whyWrong.2: An independent guest kernel is characteristic of a VM rather than an ordinary container.
whyWrong.3: VLAN forwarding does not select operating-system kernels.

questions.prompt: Two site gateways protect traffic between private LANs across an untrusted transit. The outer packet identifies the gateways while the original host-to-host IP packet is protected inside ESP. Which description fits?
options: Remote-access VPN using transport mode between the two endpoint laptops
Site-to-site IPsec using tunnel mode between the gateways
Site-to-site ESP transport mode hiding the entire original IP header
A routed VLAN trunk whose 802.1Q tag encrypts the original packet
questions.explanation: Tunnel mode adds an outer IP header for the tunnel endpoints and protects the encapsulated original IP packet according to the negotiated ESP suite. The site gateways serve their LANs, which makes this site-to-site.

whyWrong.0: The described endpoints are site gateways, not individual remote-access clients.
whyWrong.2: Transport mode does not encapsulate the complete original packet under a new outer tunnel IP header in this way.
whyWrong.3: A VLAN tag carries VLAN identification; it does not provide IPsec confidentiality.

questions.prompt: You will copy a lab router configuration with SCP to an approved server for the first time. Its SSH host-key fingerprint differs from the value supplied through your trusted inventory. Which action is appropriate?
options: Accept the offered key because SCP encrypts any server connection automatically
Stop the transfer and verify the server identity through a trusted channel before accepting a key
Use plain FTP to avoid the SSH identity check
Delete the expected fingerprint and retry with host-key checking disabled
questions.explanation: Encryption alone does not identify the intended server. An unexpected key can result from a legitimate change or a different endpoint; resolve it through a trusted channel before sending the configuration.

whyWrong.0: An encrypted connection to an unverified endpoint can still deliver the file to the wrong system.
whyWrong.2: Changing to unprotected transfer does not establish the intended server identity.
whyWrong.3: Disabling the check removes the evidence needed to authenticate the server.

questions.prompt: R1 and R2 have an OSPFv3 adjacency over a link using FE80::1 and FE80::2, and R1 learns the intended IPv6 /64 through that link. Both router IDs are distinct dotted-decimal values. Which observation is normal?
options: A dotted-decimal router ID requires IPv4 OSPFv2 to carry the IPv6 route
The neighbor link-local address must be replaced by a global address before any route is usable
OSPFv3 can use IPv6 link-local neighbors while retaining a 32-bit router identifier
Two routers must use an identical router ID when their next hops are link-local
questions.explanation: OSPFv3 uses link-local addressing on ordinary IPv6 links, while its router ID remains a 32-bit identifier commonly displayed in dotted decimal. The router IDs must be unique; they do not have to be routable IPv4 interface addresses.

whyWrong.0: The display format of the identifier does not change the routing protocol’s IPv6 function.
whyWrong.1: The outgoing link disambiguates a link-local next hop.
whyWrong.3: A shared router ID creates ambiguity rather than a required neighbor relationship.

questions.prompt: DHCP clients pass DAI, but an authorized statically addressed printer is rejected. Its IP/MAC are confirmed in the approved inventory, and no DHCP snooping binding exists for it. Which design best preserves inspection?
options: Disable DAI for the entire VLAN; permit static and dynamic hosts without further ARP validation
Add supported static ARP validation for the verified printer; keep client ports untrusted
Trust all client access ports; continue relying on DHCP snooping to inspect their ARP messages
Point the printer at an internal DNS resolver; use its forward record as the ARP validation source
questions.explanation: A static host may have no DHCP-learned binding. Use the documented ARP ACL or other supported static validation mechanism for the verified host, then test its ARP/application traffic while maintaining the rest of the inspection boundary.

whyWrong.0: This removes validation from unrelated hosts.
whyWrong.2: DAI relies on its own trust boundary and validation data; trusting clients bypasses checks on those ingress ports.
whyWrong.3: DNS does not provide the IP-to-MAC authorization used by DAI.

questions.prompt: An application asks a controller for inventory through a documented API. The controller separately programs switches, which continue forwarding frames in hardware. Which mapping is correct?
options: Application-to-controller is southbound; every forwarded packet belongs to the management plane
Controller-to-switch is northbound; switches no longer have a data plane
Application-to-controller is northbound; switch packet forwarding remains a data-plane function
Both APIs replace IP reachability, so the controller needs no working underlying network
questions.explanation: Northbound describes the controller’s application-facing interface. Southbound interfaces face managed infrastructure. The forwarding function remains in the data plane; the API does not replace the underlay path.

whyWrong.0: The application-facing API is northbound, and ordinary packet forwarding is a data-plane task.
whyWrong.1: Device-facing control is southbound; forwarding still has to occur on the network devices.
whyWrong.3: Control and management exchanges still require a functioning transport path.

questions.prompt: Which action addresses the demonstrated link fault and restores the approved design before retesting throughput?
options: Raise the IP MTU at both ends, then repeat the transfer and check whether late collisions stop
Replace the default route, then repeat the transfer without changing either endpoint link setting
Restore the approved auto settings at both capable ends; verify duplex, fresh counters and the transfer
Force full duplex on the switch only; retain the current NIC configuration without checking negotiation
questions.explanation: The settings and negotiated result establish a duplex mismatch: the forced peer does not negotiate duplex, and the auto side has fallen back to half duplex. The approved design uses negotiation at both capable ends. Retest counter deltas and the original transfer after alignment.

whyWrong.0: Late collisions concern the Ethernet link; they do not establish an IP MTU problem.
whyWrong.1: A healthy route cannot compensate for the observed local duplex mismatch.
whyWrong.3: Matching forced full duplex may remove the mismatch, but it does not restore the specified auto design or verify the resulting state.

exhibit.title: Authored evidence for this case
exhibit.text:
Approved design: both capable NIC and switch port use autonegotiation.
NIC configuration: forced 100 Mb/s, full duplex.
SW1 port: auto speed/duplex; operational 100 Mb/s, half duplex.
During the same transfer, switch late-collision counters increase. Cable test passes.

questions.prompt: A user still reaches the retired server. Which explanation and next check best fit the records?
options: The recursive answer is cached; wait for its remaining TTL or clear only the authorized cache, then query again
The authoritative server must still contain the old A record because every resolver always agrees immediately
The MX record controls this web connection and must point to the new address
A PTR update is required before an A record can be used by a browser
questions.explanation: The authoritative answer already has the approved address; the recursive resolver has an older answer with time remaining. Track expiry or perform an authorized targeted cache refresh, then confirm a new lookup and application request. Repeatedly editing correct authoritative data does not remove an existing cache entry.

whyWrong.1: Caches can retain a previous answer until its TTL expires.
whyWrong.2: Mail exchanger selection is not used for this ordinary web hostname lookup.
whyWrong.3: Reverse lookup is not a prerequisite for the displayed forward A answer.

exhibit.title: Authored evidence for this case
exhibit.text:
Approved portal.example.test IPv4 address: 192.0.2.25
Authoritative query now: A 192.0.2.25, TTL 300
Client’s recursive resolver now: A 192.0.2.15, remaining TTL 120
HTTP to 192.0.2.25 returns the expected page.

questions.prompt: What can you report from this automation run?
options: Both devices returned current route tables because changed=0 proves success
R2’s routing table is empty because there is no stdout entry for that host
The play needs an IOS configuration module before show commands can return output
R1 returned the requested evidence; R2 needs connection troubleshooting before its routing state can be assessed
questions.explanation: R1 has command output. R2 failed before the command executed, so its routing state remains unobserved. Check inventory, reachability, credentials and the indicated connection error before a scoped retry. changed=0 alone is neither proof of successful collection nor a security guarantee.

whyWrong.0: The unreachable result means the R2 command did not execute.
whyWrong.1: Missing output after a connection failure does not describe the device’s route table.
whyWrong.2: Operational show commands can be executed through ios_command without using ios_config.

exhibit.title: Authored evidence for this case
exhibit.text:
Task: cisco.ios.ios_command, commands: [show ip route]
R1: ok; stdout contains connected and OSPF routes
R2: UNREACHABLE; SSH connection timed out; no command output
Recap: R1 ok=1 changed=0 unreachable=0; R2 ok=0 changed=0 unreachable=1

questions.prompt: Which narrowly scoped edit restores the approved policy?
options: Remove sequence 10 only; retain the specific deny and final permit, then test both blocked HTTP and permitted ICMP
Remove sequence 20 only; the first permit already keeps the client reachable
Move sequence 20 after sequence 30 so the default permit is evaluated first
Change sequence 20 to deny ip any any and keep sequence 10 ahead of it
questions.explanation: The first entry permits every packet from the client subnet, including HTTP, before the specific deny is reached. Removing that unintended broad permit lets the existing specific deny and final permit express the requirement. New TCP/80 and ICMP tests check both policy outcomes.

whyWrong.1: Removing the intended deny further departs from the required service restriction.
whyWrong.2: A later deny cannot override a preceding permit.
whyWrong.3: The first broad permit would still win, and the broader deny would also affect other sources.

exhibit.title: Authored evidence for this case
exhibit.text:
Approved policy: deny TCP/80 from 172.20.40.0/24 to 10.220.30.10; allow its other IPv4 traffic.
ACL inbound on the client subinterface:
10 permit ip 172.20.40.0 0.0.0.255 any
20 deny tcp 172.20.40.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.220.30.10 eq 80
30 permit ip any any
New client HTTP succeeds and increments line 10; line 20 remains unchanged.

questions.prompt: Which dependency should be investigated next for the affected WLAN?
options: Delete and recreate the saved WPA2 profile before collecting evidence beyond the completed key exchange
Test the client’s DNS resolver before checking whether the client obtained usable IP parameters
Adjust the radio channel first, without examining the newly selected VLAN’s forwarding and DHCP path
Trace the new VLAN 30 mapping, forwarding and gateway/relay path to the DHCP server
questions.explanation: Association and key exchange have completed, and the client obtains a valid lease on a different WLAN. The affected WLAN is mapped to a newly introduced VLAN without observed DHCP replies. Trace that VLAN’s forwarding, gateway/relay and server path rather than restarting security configuration.

whyWrong.0: The completed key exchange and current no-Offer stage direct the next check beyond the saved security profile.
whyWrong.1: The client has not obtained usable addressing. First establish the DHCP path before diagnosing name resolution.
whyWrong.2: No radio fault is demonstrated, while the changed VLAN and missing DHCP replies identify a more relevant next boundary.

exhibit.title: Authored evidence for this case
exhibit.text:
WLAN LAB-STAFF: client associated; WPA2 key exchange successful; mapped to VLAN 30.
Client: repeated DHCP Discover, no Offer; no static address configured.
Same client on LAB-TEST/VLAN 10 obtains a lease and browses normally.
Change record: LAB-STAFF was remapped from VLAN 10 to VLAN 30.

cards.front: Does a course readiness score estimate Cisco’s passing score?
cards.back: No. Use it to prioritize revision and retain per-objective evidence; it is not a calibrated pass probability or official grading scale.

cards.front: Why record a correct guess as a revision gap?
cards.back: A correct option without a defensible reason is weak evidence of understanding. Rework the decision with changed values and explain why the alternatives fail.

cards.front: What makes a repeated lab attempt independent?
cards.back: Build or diagnose a fresh variation before opening the solution. Record the help used and preserve the first result separately from the corrected result.

cards.front: How should an exam objective guide a practice task?
cards.back: Match its verb: describe and compare need clear explanations; configure, verify and troubleshoot need device or packet evidence. Check the blueprint version for your appointment.

cards.front: What should follow a narrowly scoped repair?
cards.back: Repeat the original failed service test, check a permitted control and any required denial, then record the new state. An accepted command is not the same as restored service.

cards.front: How do you distinguish an unperformed check from a failed check?
cards.back: Unperformed means no evidence was collected; failed means the stated test was run and did not meet its condition. Record unsupported simulator features separately and revisit them on a suitable platform.

cards.front: What belongs in a useful mistake record?
cards.back: The objective, your original reasoning, the evidence you missed, the corrected rule and a fresh task to attempt later. Copying the answer alone does not show what changed in your reasoning.

cards.front: How should blueprint weight affect a revision plan?
cards.back: Combine the weight with demonstrated gaps and available time. A high-weight weak domain deserves attention, but smaller domains still need coverage; a weighted course score is not a pass probability.

cards.front: Why are mixed questions useful near the end of preparation?
cards.back: They require choosing the relevant concept without a chapter heading supplying it. Use unfamiliar values and explain your first choice before reading feedback.

cards.front: Which source should settle an exam-day logistics question?
cards.back: The current Cisco policy, Pearson VUE program page and your appointment instructions. Check the delivery mode and date; do not turn a course note into a permanent rule.

commands.task: Display IPv4 interface addresses and administrative/line-protocol state in brief form.
commands.note: Useful for interface state; up/up does not establish a correct VLAN path, mask or end-to-end service.

commands.task: Display the switch’s brief VLAN table with names, status and listed ports.
commands.note: Use trunk output as well; a VLAN appearing here does not prove it crosses the uplink.

commands.task: Display operational trunk ports with native, allowed and forwarding VLAN details.
commands.note: Compare configuration and physical/operational state if a planned trunk is missing.

commands.task: Display EtherChannel protocol, logical state and member flags.
commands.note: SU denotes Layer 2 in use; RU denotes Layer 3 in use. Read the legend and actual design.

commands.task: Inspect the root/bridge IDs and port roles for VLAN 10.
commands.note: Compare the full IDs and this bridge’s root indication; then examine costs, roles and forwarding state.

commands.task: Display the installed IPv4 routing table.
commands.note: For an ordinary destination lookup, find the longest matching prefix; use the default only when no longer prefix matches.

commands.task: Display OSPFv2 neighbors and their state, timer and interface.
commands.note: FULL is expected for the intended adjacency. Two DROTHER routers may normally remain 2WAY on a broadcast segment.

commands.task: Display current NAT/PAT translation entries.
commands.note: An empty table can reflect no eligible recent traffic, expiry or several configuration/path faults.

commands.task: Display the IOS DHCP server’s current bindings.
commands.note: A missing binding is not proof that no Discover arrived; a present binding is not proof every client option is correct.

commands.task: Display configured IPv4 ACL entries and their available match counters.
commands.note: Compare before/after fresh traffic. An unchanged later counter may mean an earlier entry matched, among other causes.

tickets.title: Small transit pings work but OSPF will not reach FULL
tickets.scenario: On an isolated Ethernet lab, R1 and R2 previously reached FULL. R1 was changed to ip mtu 1400 without a design requirement. Both NICs and the direct link support the approved 1500-byte IPv4 MTU. The router IDs are unique, area/timers match, and no mtu-ignore override is configured. Small transit pings still succeed.

exhibits.title: Representative neighbor and IP interface state
exhibits.text:
R1 neighbor 2.2.2.2: EXSTART
R1 Gi0/0/1 IP MTU: 1400
R2 Gi0/0/0 IP MTU: 1500

exhibits.title: Authored packet observation
exhibits.text:
R2 database-description packet advertises interface MTU 1500.
R1 rejects that DBD under its 1400-byte interface-MTU check.
Approved direct-link IP MTU: 1500 on both routers.

tickets.question: Which correction addresses the demonstrated failure while retaining MTU validation?
options: Reduce the OSPF hello interval only on R1
Enable ip ospf mtu-ignore at both ends
Restore R1 to the approved 1500-byte IP MTU
Give R1 the same router ID as R2
tickets.explanation: The mismatched MTU and rejection observation establish this particular database-exchange failure. A small ping does not test the same condition, and EXSTART by itself would not identify a unique cause.
tickets.fix:
Restore the documented value in this isolated lab:

```ios
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R1(config-if)# ip mtu 1500
R1(config-if)# end
R1# show ip interface gigabitethernet0/0/1
R1# show ip ospf neighbor
R1# show ip route
```

Verify the peer, required routes and application return path after convergence. On an actual constrained path, determine a mutually supported MTU from evidence rather than raising it blindly or bypassing the check. After confirming both route directions, repeat the permitted USERS/PC-A HTTP request to SRV and retain the intended STAFF/PC-B HTTP denial. Record fresh requests rather than relying on an old page.

tickets.title: Clients cannot renew after a switch security change
tickets.scenario: After DHCP snooping is enabled for VLAN 20, client renewal fails while static clients still communicate. The approved DHCP server is reachable only through SW2 Gi0/1. The collected evidence explicitly identifies a legitimate server OFFER arriving there and being discarded; endpoint ports should remain untrusted.

exhibits.title: Representative configuration
exhibits.text:
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan 20
interface GigabitEthernet0/1
 switchport mode trunk
 ! no ip dhcp snooping trust configured

exhibits.title: Authored observation record
exhibits.text:
Snooping operational VLANs: 20
Client DISCOVER: leaves Gi0/1 toward approved server
Legitimate DHCPOFFER: received on Gi0/1
Drop reason: DHCP server message on untrusted ingress port

tickets.question: Which correction matches the evidence without trusting clients?
options: Disable snooping globally on every switch
Trust the verified server-facing Gi0/1 ingress
Trust every VLAN 20 client access port
Change the working client gateway to the server
tickets.explanation: The observed OFFER is rejected on the verified server-facing ingress because it remains untrusted. The server has already responded, so an unproven claim that option 82 prevented every response does not explain this observation.
tickets.fix:
After confirming Gi0/1’s physical and logical path to the approved server, configure that interface:

```ios
SW2# configure terminal
SW2(config)# interface gigabitethernet0/1
SW2(config-if)# ip dhcp snooping trust
SW2(config-if)# end
SW2# show ip dhcp snooping
```
